sentences.zh: 列傳第六十五

translations.literal: Biographies 65
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 65

sentences.zh: 裴政李諤鮑宏高構榮毗陸知命梁毗柳彧趙綽杜整

translations.literal: Pei Zheng Li E Bao Hong Gao Gou Rong Pi Lu Zhiming Lian Pi Liu Yu Zhao Chao Du Zheng
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zheng, Li E, Bao Hong, Gao Gou, Rong Pi, Lu Zhiming, Lian Pi, Liu Yu, Zhao Chao, and Du Zheng

sentences.zh: 裴政，字德表，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Zheng, courtesy name Debiao, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zheng, styled Debiao, came from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖邃，父之禮，並《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sui and his father Zhili both have biographies in the Nanshi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Pei Sui and his father Pei Zhili both have entries in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 政幼聰明，博聞強記，達于從政，為當世所稱。

translations.literal: From childhood Zheng was bright and intelligent, broad in learning and strong in memory, skilled in governance, and praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was clever from boyhood, widely read with a formidable memory, adept at public affairs, and acclaimed in his own time.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，以軍功封為夷陵侯，給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He served in Liang and, for military merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yiling and appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he won military honors, was made Marquis of Yiling, and served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 及魏軍圍荊州，政在外見獲，蕭察謂政曰：「我，武皇帝之孫，不可為爾君乎？

translations.literal: When Wei armies besieged Jingzhou, Zheng was captured outside the city. Xiao Cha said to Zheng: "I am the grandson of Emperor Wu — will you not serve me as your lord?
translations.idiomatic: When Wei forces besieged Jingzhou, Zheng was taken captive outside the walls. Xiao Cha told him, "I am Emperor Wu's grandson — will you not accept me as your sovereign?

sentences.zh: 爾何煩殉身于七父。

translations.literal: Why do you trouble yourself to die for your seventh uncle?
translations.idiomatic: Why must you throw your life away for your seventh uncle?

sentences.zh: 若從我計，則貴及子孫，不然，分腰領矣。

translations.literal: If you follow my plan, honor will reach your descendants; if not, your waist and neck will be severed.
translations.idiomatic: Follow my counsel and wealth will reach your children and grandchildren; refuse, and I will cut you in two.

sentences.zh: 」鎖之，送至城下，使謂元帝曰：「王僧辯聞台城破，已自為帝。

translations.literal: " They chained him and brought him to the foot of the wall, ordering him to tell Emperor Yuan: "Wang Sengbian heard that the capital had fallen and has already proclaimed himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " They bound him and led him beneath the walls, instructing him to tell Emperor Yuan, "Wang Sengbian, hearing the capital had fallen, has already declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 王琳孤弱，不能復來。

translations.literal: Wang Lin is isolated and weak and cannot come again.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin stands alone and is too weak to return.

sentences.zh: 」政許之。

translations.literal: " Zheng agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng assented.

sentences.zh: 既而告城中曰：「援兵大至，吾以間使被禽，當以碎身報國。

translations.literal: Then he told those in the city: "Relief troops are arriving in great force. Because I was captured while serving as a secret messenger, I shall repay the state with my broken body.
translations.idiomatic: But then he shouted to the city, "Reinforcements are near! Though I was seized while carrying a secret message, I will repay the realm with my shattered body.

sentences.zh: 監者擊其口，終不易辭。

translations.literal: His guards struck his mouth, but in the end he did not change his words.
translations.idiomatic: The guards struck his mouth, yet he never altered his statement.

sentences.zh: 察怒，命趣行戮。

translations.literal: Cha was enraged and ordered him hurried to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Cha ordered him taken at once for execution.

sentences.zh: 蔡大業諫曰：「此人之望也，殺之，則荊州不可下。

translations.literal: Cai Daye remonstrated: "This man is one the people look up to — if you kill him, Jingzhou cannot be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Daye urged him: "This man commands public esteem — kill him, and you will never take Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 因得釋。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was released.
translations.idiomatic: On that account he was spared.

sentences.zh: 會江陵平，與城中朝士俱送京師。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he was sent to the capital together with the court officials of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling was pacified, he was sent to the capital along with the city's court officials.

sentences.zh: 周文聞其忠，援員外散騎侍郎，引入相府。

translations.literal: Wen of Zhou, hearing of his loyalty, appointed him Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and brought him into the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou, learning of his fidelity, made him Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and brought him into the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 命與盧辯依《周禮》建六官，並攢次朝儀，車服器用，多遵古禮，革漢、魏之法，事並施行。

translations.literal: He was ordered, together with Lu Bian, to establish the six offices according to the Rites of Zhou, and also to compile court ritual, chariots, dress, and implements — for the most part following ancient rites and reforming Han and Wei law; all these matters were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He and Lu Bian were charged to erect the six ministries after the Rites of Zhou, to codify court ceremony, carriages, dress, and regalia — largely reviving ancient practice and overturning Han and Wei custom — and all of it was put into effect.

sentences.zh: 尋授刑部下大夫，轉少司憲。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Master of the Ministry of Punishments and transferred to Junior Director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became Grand Master of the Ministry of Punishments, then Junior Director of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 政明習故事，又參定周律。

translations.literal: Zheng was well versed in precedent and also participated in drafting the Zhou code.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng knew precedent thoroughly and helped draft the Zhou legal code.

sentences.zh: 能飲酒，至數斗不亂。

translations.literal: He could drink wine — even several dou without losing composure.
translations.idiomatic: He could hold his wine — several dou without disorder.

sentences.zh: 簿案盈幾，剖決如流，用法寬平，無有冤濫。

translations.literal: Legal dossiers piled on his desk, yet he decided cases like flowing water; his application of the law was lenient and fair, with no wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Case files stacked his desk, yet he judged like running water; his law was lenient and even, and no innocent suffered.

sentences.zh: 囚徒犯極刑者，乃許其妻子入獄就之。

translations.literal: For prisoners facing the death penalty, he even permitted their wives and children to enter the prison to be with them.
translations.idiomatic: Even for those condemned to death he allowed wives and children into the prison to stay with them.

sentences.zh: 至冬，將行決，皆曰：「裴大夫致我于死，死無所恨。

translations.literal: When winter came and executions were to be carried out, all said: "Vice Minister Pei brought us to death — we die without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When winter brought the executions, each said, "Vice Minister Pei has brought us to this — we die without complaint.

sentences.zh: 」又善鐘律，嘗與長孫紹遠論樂，事在《紹遠傳》。

translations.literal: " He was also skilled in bells and pitch pipes; once he debated music with Zhangsun Shaoyuan — the matter is in the biography of Shaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: " He was also versed in bells and pitch standards; he once debated music with Zhangsun Shaoyuan, as recorded in Shaoyuan's biography.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇元年，為率更令，加上儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang of Sui, he became Director of the Directorate of Astronomy and was given the additional title of Third Rank Commissioner with Distinction.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui's first Kaihuang year he became Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, with the added rank of Third Rank Commissioner with Distinction.

sentences.zh: 詔與蘇威等修定律令。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him, together with Su Wei and others, to revise the laws and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order set him, with Su Wei and others, to revise statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 采魏、晉刑典，下至齊、梁，沿革輕重，取其折衷。

translations.literal: They drew on Wei and Jin penal codes down through Qi and Liang, tracing changes in severity and weight, and chose a middle course.
translations.idiomatic: They drew on Wei and Jin penal law down through Qi and Liang, weighing shifts in severity, and struck a balanced mean.

sentences.zh: 同撰著者十餘人，凡疑滯不通，皆取決於政。

translations.literal: More than ten co-authors worked on it; wherever doubts blocked progress, the decision rested with Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten men co-authored the work; wherever a knot of doubt remained, Zheng's word settled it.

sentences.zh: 進位散騎常侍，轉左庶子。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and transferred to Left Chief of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Palace Attendant and became Left Chief of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 多所匡正，見稱純愨，東宮凡有大事，皆以委之。

translations.literal: He corrected many things and was praised for integrity and sincerity; for all major affairs of the Eastern Palace, the crown prince entrusted them to him.
translations.idiomatic: He corrected much and was praised for plain integrity; the crown prince entrusted all weighty Eastern Palace business to him.

sentences.zh: 右庶子劉榮，性甚專固。

translations.literal: The Right Chief of the Household Liu Rong was by nature very stubborn and inflexible.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rong, Right Chief of the Household, was by nature rigid and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 時武職交番，通事舍人趙元愷作辭見帳，未及成。

translations.literal: At that time military officers were rotating in turn; Master for Communications Zhao Yuankai was drafting a written roster for the oral audience but had not finished it.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers were then rotating duty; Master for Communications Zhao Yuankai was drafting a written name roster for the audience but had not finished.

sentences.zh: 太子再三催促，榮令元愷口奏，不須造帳。

translations.literal: The crown prince repeatedly pressed him; Rong ordered Yuankai to present orally and said there was no need to prepare a roster.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince pressed him again and again; Rong told Yuankai to report orally and said no roster was needed.

sentences.zh: 及奏，太子問：「名帳安在？

translations.literal: When the presentation was made, the crown prince asked: "Where is the name roster?
translations.idiomatic: When the report was given, the crown prince asked, "Where is the name roster?

sentences.zh: 」元愷云：「稟承劉榮，不聽造帳。

translations.literal: " Yuankai said: "I received instruction from Liu Rong — I was not allowed to prepare a roster.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuankai replied, "Liu Rong instructed me — I was forbidden to make one.

sentences.zh: 」太子即以詰榮，榮便拒諱，太子付政推問。

translations.literal: " The crown prince immediately questioned Rong; Rong tried to deny it, and the crown prince entrusted the investigation to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince at once confronted Rong, who denied it; the crown prince handed the inquiry to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 未及奏狀，阿附榮者先言于太子曰：「政欲陷榮，推事不實。

translations.literal: Before the report was submitted, those who sided with Rong spoke first to the crown prince: "Zheng wants to frame Rong — his investigation is not based on fact.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zheng could report, Rong's allies told the crown prince, "Zheng means to trap Rong — his inquiry is unfounded.

sentences.zh: 」太子召責之，政曰：「凡推事有兩，一察情，一據證，審其曲直，以定是非。

translations.literal: The crown prince summoned and reproached him. Zheng said: "In any investigation there are two [approaches]: one is to examine the circumstances, one is to rely on evidence — examine right and wrong to determine what is true and false.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince summoned and rebuked him. Zheng said, "Every inquiry has two sides: reading the circumstances and weighing the proof — then judging right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 臣察榮位高任重，縱實語元愷，蓋是纖介之愆，計不須諱。

translations.literal: I examined Rong's circumstances: his position is high and his responsibility great; even if he truly spoke to Yuankai, it would merely be a petty fault — I think there is no need to deny it.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Rong's situation — high rank, heavy duty — even if he truly spoke to Yuankai, it would be a trifling lapse, hardly worth denying.

sentences.zh: 又察元愷，受制于榮，豈敢以無端之言妄相點累。

translations.literal: I also examined Yuankai: controlled by Rong, how could he dare to use groundless words to falsely implicate him?
translations.idiomatic: Reading Yuankai — under Rong's thumb — how could he invent a charge without cause?

sentences.zh: 二人之情理正相似。

translations.literal: The circumstances of the two men are exactly similar.
translations.idiomatic: Their circumstances point the same way.

sentences.zh: 元愷引左衛率崔茜等證，茜款狀悉與元愷符同。

translations.literal: Yuankai cited Left Guard Leader Cui Qian and others as witnesses; Qian's confession matched Yuankai's in every particular.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai called Left Guard Leader Cui Qian and others; Qian's testimony matched Yuankai's in full.

sentences.zh: 察情既敵，須以證定。

translations.literal: Since the circumstances are equal, one must decide by evidence.
translations.idiomatic: With circumstances evenly matched, proof must decide.

sentences.zh: 臣謂榮語元愷非虛。

translations.literal: I say Rong's words to Yuankai were not false.
translations.idiomatic: I conclude Rong did speak to Yuankai.

sentences.zh: 」太子亦不罪榮，而稱政平直。

translations.literal: " The crown prince did not punish Rong either, and praised Zheng for his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince did not punish Rong, and praised Zheng for his evenhandedness.

sentences.zh: 政好面折人短，而退無後言。

translations.literal: Zheng liked to rebuke people to their faces for their faults, but after withdrawing he made no further comment.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng liked to confront others with their faults face to face, yet never spoke of them again once he had withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 時雲定興數入侍太子，為奇服異器，進奉後宮，又緣女寵，來往無節。

translations.literal: At that time Yun Dingxing frequently attended the crown prince, bringing bizarre dress and unusual objects as offerings to the inner palace, and also, relying on his daughter's favor, came and went without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Dingxing then often attended the crown prince, sending exotic garments and curios to the inner palace and, trading on his daughter's favor, passing in and out without restraint.

sentences.zh: 政數切諫，太子不納。

translations.literal: Zheng repeatedly remonstrated sharply, but the crown prince did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng admonished him repeatedly, but the crown prince would not listen.

sentences.zh: 政謂定興曰：「公所為不合禮度。

translations.literal: Zheng said to Dingxing: "Your conduct does not accord with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng told Dingxing, "Your behavior violates ritual decorum.

sentences.zh: 又元妃暴薨，道路籍籍，此于太子非令名也。

translations.literal: Moreover the primary consort died suddenly — rumors fill the streets; this is no good name for the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The crown princess died suddenly, and gossip fills the streets — this does the crown prince no credit.

sentences.zh: 願公自引退，不然將及禍。

translations.literal: I hope you will withdraw of your own accord; otherwise disaster will overtake you.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw of your own will, or calamity will find you.

sentences.zh: 」定興怒，以告太子，太子益疏政。

translations.literal: " Dingxing was angry and told the crown prince; the crown prince grew ever more distant from Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: " Dingxing complained to the crown prince, who grew ever colder toward Zheng.

sentences.zh: 由是出為襄州總管，妻子不之官，所受秩奉，散給僚吏。

translations.literal: For this reason he was sent out as Inspector-General of Xiangzhou; his wife and children did not accompany him to his post, and the salary he received he distributed among his staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: On that account he was posted as Inspector-General of Xiangzhou; his family did not go with him, and he gave his stipend to his staff.

sentences.zh: 人犯罪者，陰悉知之，或竟歲不發，至再三犯，乃因都會時，於眾中召出，親案其罪，五人處死，流、徒者甚眾。

translations.literal: When people committed crimes, he secretly knew it all; sometimes he did not expose it for a whole year — only when they offended again and again would he, at a public gathering, summon them forth, personally examine their guilt; five were put to death, and those banished or transported were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When men broke the law he often knew in secret; sometimes he waited a full year without acting — only after repeated offenses would he, at a public assembly, call them out, judge them himself, execute five, and banish or transport many more.

sentences.zh: 合境惶懾，令行禁止，稱為神明，爾後不修囹圄，殆無諍訟。

translations.literal: The whole jurisdiction was fearful and in awe; orders were enforced and prohibitions obeyed — he was called a divine official; thereafter he scarcely maintained the prisons, and there were almost no lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: The whole region trembled; his orders ran and his bans held — men called him a spirit in office; afterward he barely kept the jails in repair, and lawsuits nearly vanished.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 著《承聖實錄》十卷。

translations.literal: He wrote the Shésheng Shilu in ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Veritable Record of the Shésheng reign in ten fascicles.

sentences.zh: 及太子廢，文帝追憶之曰：「向遣裴政、劉行本在，共匡弼之，猶應不令至此。」

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, Emperor Wen recalled with regret: "If Pei Zheng and Liu Xingben had been kept here to assist and correct him, it still should not have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed, Emperor Wen looked back in sorrow: "Had Pei Zheng and Liu Xingben remained to guide him, things might never have reached this pass.

sentences.zh: 子南金，位膳部郎，學涉有文藻，以輕財貴義稱。

translations.literal: His son Nanjin held the post of Director in the Board of Provisions; broad in learning and skilled in literary composition, he was known for valuing righteousness over wealth.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nanjin served as Director in the Board of Provisions — learned, literary, and known for prizing integrity over money.

sentences.zh: 李諤，字士恢，趙郡人也。

translations.literal: Li E, courtesy name Shihui, was a native of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li E, styled Shihui, was from Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 博學解屬文。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely learned and adept at writing.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，為中書舍人，有口辯，每接對陳使。

translations.literal: He served in Qi as Master of Documents in the Secretariat and was eloquent — whenever envoys from Chen arrived he received them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he was Secretariat Master of Documents, quick of tongue — he always received Chen envoys.

sentences.zh: 周平齊，拜天官都上士。

translations.literal: When Zhou conquered Qi, he was appointed Director of the Heavenly Office, Senior Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou conquered Qi, he was made Senior Clerk in the Directorate of the Heavenly Office.

sentences.zh: 諤見隋文帝有帝王志操，深自結納。

translations.literal: E saw that Emperor Wen of Sui had the will and capacity of an emperor and formed a deep personal bond with him.
translations.idiomatic: E saw in Emperor Wen of Sui the mettle of a true sovereign and drew close to him.

sentences.zh: 及帝為丞相，甚見親待，訪以得失。

translations.literal: When the emperor became Chancellor, E was greatly favored and trusted; the emperor consulted him on successes and failures.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor became Chancellor, E won deep trust; the emperor asked his counsel on what had gone right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 時兵革屢動，國用虛耗，諤上《重穀論》以諷焉。

translations.literal: At that time military campaigns were frequent and state revenues were depleted; E submitted the "Treatise on Valuing Grain" as a subtle admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Wars came one after another and the treasury ran dry; E submitted his "Treatise on Valuing Grain" as a veiled remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，曆比部、考功二曹侍郎，賜爵南和伯。

translations.literal: After the accession, he successively served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Personnel, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanhe.
translations.idiomatic: After the founding of Sui he served in turn as Vice Director of Justice and of Personnel, and was made Baron of Nanhe.

sentences.zh: 諤性公方，明時務。

translations.literal: E was by nature upright and public-spirited, and understood the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: E was upright by nature, clear-eyed about the times.

sentences.zh: 遷書侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Secretary and Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Palace Secretary and Censor.

sentences.zh: 上謂群臣曰：「朕昔為大司馬，每求外職，李諤陳十二策，苦勸不許，朕遂決意在內。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the assembled ministers: "When I was formerly Grand Commandant, I repeatedly sought an outside appointment — Li E presented twelve stratagems and strenuously urged me not to permit it; I then resolved to remain within.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "When I was Grand Commandant I often wanted an outside post; Li E laid out twelve arguments and pressed me to stay — and I chose to remain at court.

sentences.zh: 今此事業，諤之力也。

translations.literal: The enterprise we have today is largely due to E's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: What we have built today owes much to E.

sentences.zh: 」賜物二千段。

translations.literal: " He was granted two thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: " He was rewarded with two thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 諤見禮教凋弊，公卿薨亡，其愛妾侍婢，子孫輒嫁賣之，遂成風俗，乃上書曰：「臣聞追遠慎終，人德歸厚，三年無改，方稱為孝。

translations.literal: E saw that ritual instruction was in decline; when ministers and high officials died, their beloved concubines and maidservants were promptly married off or sold by their descendants — this had become custom — and he submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that in honoring the distant and handling the end carefully, human virtue returns to depth; three years without change — only then is one called filial.
translations.idiomatic: E saw ritual decay: when great ministers died, heirs at once sold or married off favored concubines and maids — a custom grown common — and he memorialized: "I have heard that honoring the dead and minding the end deepens human virtue; only one who keeps mourning three years unchanged may be called filial.

sentences.zh: 如聞大臣之內，有父祖亡沒，日月未久，子孫無賴，引其妓妾，嫁賣取財，有一於此，實損風化。

translations.literal: I hear that among chief ministers, there are those whose fathers and grandfathers have recently died — within no great time their worthless descendants bring out their singing-girls and concubines and marry or sell them for cash; where this occurs even once, it truly damages prevailing custom.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that among high ministers, scarcely after a father's or grandfather's death, worthless sons drag out singing-girls and concubines and sell or marry them for coin — even once, this corrodes public morals.

sentences.zh: 妾雖微賤，親承衣履，服斬三年，古今通式。

translations.literal: Though concubines are lowly, they personally received one's robes and shoes — three years of deep mourning is the universal formula, ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: Concubines, though low in rank, wore their master's clothes — three years of deepest mourning is the rule in every age.

sentences.zh: 豈容遽褫衰絰，強傅鉛華，泣辭靈幾之前，送付他人之室？

translations.literal: How can one abruptly strip off the mourning hemp and forcibly apply rouge and powder — weeping before the spirit couch and then delivering them to another man's house?
translations.idiomatic: How can one tear off mourning cloth, force on paint and powder, weep before the bier — then send a woman to another man's bed?

sentences.zh: 凡在見者，猶致傷心，況乎人子，能堪斯忍！

translations.literal: Even those who merely witnessed it were still wounded at heart — how much more sons of men, who could bear such cruelty!
translations.idiomatic: Even bystanders are cut to the heart — what son could endure it?

sentences.zh: 復有朝廷重臣，位望通貴，平生交舊，情若弟兄。

translations.literal: There are also weighty court ministers, of eminent rank and widespread honor, who in life were close friends — affection like brothers.
translations.idiomatic: There are great courtiers of lofty rank who in life were sworn friends, close as brothers.

sentences.zh: 及其亡沒，杳同行路，朝聞其死，夕規其妾，方便求娉，以得為限。

translations.literal: When such men die, they are as remote as strangers on the road: in the morning one hears of the death, by evening one plots for his concubine — seizing every opening to seek marriage, limited only by what one can obtain.
translations.idiomatic: When such a man dies they become strangers: morning brings word of death, evening brings a bid for his concubine — every chance seized, every match pursued.

sentences.zh: 無廉恥之心，棄友朋之義。

translations.literal: No sense of shame — casting aside the obligations of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: No shame — friendship cast aside.

sentences.zh: 且居家理務，可移於官，既不正私，何能贊務？

translations.literal: Moreover the management of a household can be transferred to office — if one is not upright in private life, how can one assist in public affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Household conduct mirrors public duty — if a man is crooked at home, how can he serve the state?

sentences.zh: 」上覽而嘉之。

translations.literal: " The emperor read it and approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor read it and praised it.

sentences.zh: 五品已上妻妾不得改醮，始於此也。

translations.literal: The rule that wives and concubines of officials of the fifth rank and above must not remarry began from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this came the ban on remarriage for wives and concubines of fifth-rank officials and above.

sentences.zh: 諤又以時文體尚輕薄，流宕忘反，上書曰：

translations.literal: E also saw that literary style of the time favored the frivolous and light — drifting away without return — and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: E also saw the age's writing grow frivolous — drifting ever further — and submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞古先哲王之化人也，必變其視聽，防其嗜欲，塞其邪放之心，示以淳和之路。

translations.literal: I have heard that when the sage kings of antiquity transformed men, they necessarily changed what they saw and heard, guarded against their appetites and desires, blocked the heart's wayward impulses, and showed them the path of pure harmony.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that sage kings of old, in shaping men, altered sight and hearing, checked appetite and desire, sealed off wayward hearts, and pointed the way to simple harmony.

sentences.zh: 五教六行，為訓人之本，《詩》、《書》、《禮》、《易》，為道義之門。

translations.literal: The Five Teachings and Six Conducts are the root of instructing men; the Book of Songs, Book of Documents, Rites, and Changes are the gates of moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Teachings and Six Conducts are the root of instruction; the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Changes are the gates of right conduct.

sentences.zh: 故能家復孝慈，人知禮讓，正俗調風，莫大於此。

translations.literal: Thus households restore filial piety and kindness, people know ritual and modesty — nothing greater than this for correcting custom and harmonizing manners.
translations.idiomatic: Thus families recover filial kindness, people learn ritual and forbearance — nothing better reforms custom and tunes the wind of the age.

sentences.zh: 其有上書獻賦，制誄鐫銘，皆以褒德序賢，明勳證理。

translations.literal: For those who submit memorials, present rhapsodies, compose eulogies, or inscribe steles — all praise virtue and arrange the worthy, making merit clear and principle evident.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials, rhapsodies, dirges, and inscriptions all exalt virtue, set forth the worthy, and make merit and principle plain.

sentences.zh: 苟非懲勸，義不徒然。

translations.literal: If not for warning and encouragement, the meaning would not be in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Unless meant to warn and exhort, their purpose would be empty.

sentences.zh: 降及後代，風教漸落。

translations.literal: Down to later generations, customs and instruction gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, teaching and custom waned.

sentences.zh: 魏之三祖，更尚文詞，忽君人之大道，好雕蟲之小藝。

translations.literal: The three founders of Wei came to favor literary phrasing, neglecting the great Way of rulership and delighting in the lesser craft of ornamental writing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's three founding emperors turned to polished phrasing, neglecting the ruler's great Way and cherishing the small art of ornament.

sentences.zh: 下之從上，有同影響，競騁文華，遂成風俗。

translations.literal: The lower follows the upper like shadow follows form — racing to display literary elegance until it became custom.
translations.idiomatic: Lower ranks mirrored the upper like shadow to body — all raced for literary display until it became habit.

sentences.zh: 江左齊、梁，其弊彌甚，貴賤賢愚，唯務吟詠。

translations.literal: In the Jiangzuo of Qi and Liang the abuse was even worse — noble and base, worthy and foolish, all devoted themselves solely to composing verse.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi and Liang south of the Yangtze the rot ran deeper — high and low, wise and dull, all wrote poetry and nothing else.

sentences.zh: 遂復遺理存異，尋虛逐微，競一韻之奇，爭一字之巧。

translations.literal: Again they abandoned principle and preserved anomaly, sought the hollow and pursued the minute — competing for the marvel of a single rhyme, contending for the cleverness of a single character.
translations.idiomatic: They forsook substance for novelty, chased the hollow and the fine — vying for one startling rhyme, one clever word.

sentences.zh: 連篇累牘，不出月露之形，積案盈箱，唯是風雲之狀。

translations.literal: Linking fascicle to fascicle, nothing beyond the shapes of moon and dew; piling dossier upon dossier, only forms of wind and cloud.
translations.idiomatic: Page after page held nothing but moonlight and dew; dossier on dossier held only wind and cloud.

sentences.zh: 世俗以此相高，朝廷據茲擢士。

translations.literal: The world on this account held one another high, and the court on this basis promoted scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Society prized this above all, and the throne promoted men for it.

sentences.zh: 祿利之路既開，愛尚之情愈篤。

translations.literal: Once the path of salary and profit was opened, the passion for what was prized grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Once office and profit lay open, devotion to fashion only deepened.

sentences.zh: 於是閭里童昏，貴遊總卯，未窺六甲，先制五言。

translations.literal: Thus village lads and noble youths, before they had grasped the six jia, already composed five-character verse.
translations.idiomatic: Village children and noble scions, before learning their first characters, were already writing pentameter.

sentences.zh: 至如羲皇、舜、禹之典，伊、傅、周、孔之說，不復關心，何嘗入耳。

translations.literal: As for the canons of Fuxi, Yao, and Yu, or the teachings of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius — they no longer cared; how could such things ever reach their ears?
translations.idiomatic: The classics of Fuxi, Yao, and Yu, the teachings of Yi Yin, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius — they ignored them entirely; such things never reached their ears.

sentences.zh: 以傲誕為清虛，以緣情為勳績，指儒素為古拙，用詞賦為君子。

translations.literal: They took arrogant eccentricity for pure emptiness, took indulgence of sentiment for merit, called plain Confucian virtue antiquated and clumsy, and made rhapsody and fu the mark of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: They mistook insolent wit for refinement, mistook sentiment for achievement, called plain Confucian virtue crude, and made polished verse the badge of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 故文筆日繁，其政日亂，良由棄大聖之軌模，構無用以為用也。

translations.literal: Thus literary composition grew daily more elaborate while governance grew daily more chaotic — truly because they abandoned the great sage's model and built uselessness into use.
translations.idiomatic: Writing grew ever more ornate while rule grew ever more chaotic — because men cast aside the sage's pattern and made the useless their standard.

sentences.zh: 捐本逐末，流遍華壤，遞相師祖，久而愈扇。

translations.literal: Abandoning root and pursuing branch, the current spread through the civilized lands — each teaching the next, and with time the flame burned brighter.
translations.idiomatic: Root was cast aside for branch; the tide swept the realm — master after disciple, and the wind only strengthened.

sentences.zh: 及大隋受命，聖道聿興，屏黜浮詞，遏止華偽。

translations.literal: When Great Sui received the Mandate, the sage Way rose anew — frivolous phrasing was dismissed and ornate falsity was checked.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui took the throne, the sage Way revived — empty rhetoric was banished and gaudy pretense was stopped.

sentences.zh: 自非懷經抱持，志道依仁，不得引預搢紳，參廁纓冕。

translations.literal: Unless one embraced the classics and held fast to them, with will set on the Way and leaning on benevolence, one could not be admitted among the gentry or share in rank and crown.
translations.idiomatic: Only those steeped in the classics, devoted to the Way and anchored in benevolence, could enter the ranks of office and wear the court's insignia.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年，普詔天下，公私文翰，並宜實錄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaihuang, a universal edict went forth to the empire: public and private documents alike should record truth.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 4 an edict went to all the realm: every public and private document should tell the plain truth.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，泗州刺史司馬幼之文表華豔，付所司推罪。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, the literary memorial of Sima Youzhi, Prefect of Sizhou, was florid and ornate — he was handed over to the authorities for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month, Sima Youzhi of Sizhou submitted a memorial of gaudy prose — and was prosecuted for it.

sentences.zh: 自是公卿大臣感知正道，莫不鑽仰墳素，棄絕華綺，擇先王之令典，行大道於茲世。

translations.literal: From then on ministers and high officials, sensing the upright Way, all turned to the tombs of the ancients, cast off ornate silk, chose the former kings' good ordinances, and walked the great Way in this age.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter ministers, awakened to the true Way, turned to the classics, cast off ornament, took the ancient kings' laws, and walked the great Way in their own time.

sentences.zh: 如聞外州遠縣，仍踵弊風，選吏舉人，未遵典則。

translations.literal: I hear that in distant prefectures and far counties the old abuse still follows — in selecting clerks and recommending men for office, they do not follow the canon.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in remote prefectures and distant counties the old rot persists — in choosing clerks and recommending candidates, the rules are still ignored.

sentences.zh: 宗黨稱孝，鄉曲歸仁，學必典謨，交不苟合，則擯落私門，不加收齒；

translations.literal: If the clan praised one's filial piety and the neighborhood returned one to benevolence, if one's learning rested on the canon and one's associations were not casual, then one was rejected at private gates and not enrolled;
translations.idiomatic: If a man was praised for filial piety in his clan and for benevolence in his neighborhood, if his learning rested on the canon and his friendships were serious, he was turned away and not enrolled;

sentences.zh: 其學不稽古，逐俗隨時，作輕薄之篇章，結朋黨而求譽。

translations.literal: If one's learning did not examine antiquity, followed fashion with the times, wrote frivolous compositions, and formed cliques to seek reputation —
translations.idiomatic: If a man's learning ignored antiquity, chased fashion, wrote light verse, and formed factions for praise —

sentences.zh: 則選充吏職，舉送天朝。

translations.literal: Then one was chosen for clerical office and recommended to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Then he was made a clerk and sent up to the capital.

sentences.zh: 蓋由縣令、刺史，未行風教，猶挾私情，不存公道。

translations.literal: This was because the county magistrates and prefects did not carry out moral instruction, still indulged private feeling, and did not preserve public fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The cause lay with magistrates and prefects who failed to teach public morals, indulged private favor, and ignored the public good.

sentences.zh: 臣既忝憲司，職當糾察。

translations.literal: Your servant, holding office in the Censorate, has the duty to investigate and censure.
translations.idiomatic: I serve in the Censorate, charged with investigation and censure.

sentences.zh: 若聞風即劾，恐掛綱者多，請勒有司，普加搜訪，有如此者，具狀送台。

translations.literal: If I impeached on hearing of every such case, I fear too many would fall into the net — I ask that the responsible offices be ordered to search broadly; wherever such cases exist, full reports should be sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: To impeach every case at once would snare too many — I ask the responsible offices to search broadly and send full reports on every such offender to the capital.

sentences.zh: 諤又以當官者好自矜伐，復上奏具陳其弊。

translations.literal: E also saw that those in office liked to boast of their achievements, and again submitted a memorial fully stating the abuse.
translations.idiomatic: E also saw officials fond of self-praise, and submitted another memorial detailing the abuse.

sentences.zh: 請加罪黜，以懲風軌。

translations.literal: He asked that guilt be added and dismissal imposed, to warn and correct custom.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that offenders be punished and removed, to reform public conduct.

sentences.zh: 上以諤前後所奏頒示天下，四海靡然向風，深革其弊。

translations.literal: The emperor had E's successive memorials promulgated throughout the empire; the four seas turned like wind toward the Way, and the abuse was deeply reformed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor published E's memorials across the realm; the empire turned toward the Way, and the rot was deeply cut back.

sentences.zh: 諤在職數年，務存大體，不尚嚴猛，由是無剛謇之譽，而潛有匡正之志。

translations.literal: In office for several years, E kept to the larger pattern and did not favor severity — thus he won no reputation for blunt integrity, yet secretly held the will to correct.
translations.idiomatic: E served several years, keeping to broad principles rather than harsh methods — he won no fame for blunt integrity, yet quietly worked to set things right.

sentences.zh: 邳公蘇威以臨道店舍，乃求利之徒，事業汙雜，非敦本之義。

translations.literal: Duke of Pi Su Wei, regarding roadside inns as the haunts of profit-seekers — their business filthy and mixed — held that this was not the meaning of honoring the root.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Duke of Pi, held that roadside inns were haunts of profit, their trade sordid and mixed — not the way to honor fundamental values.

sentences.zh: 遂奏約遣歸農。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized that they be contracted and sent back to farming.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that innkeepers be reduced and returned to farming.

sentences.zh: 有願依舊者，在所州縣，錄附市籍，仍撤毀舊店，並令遠道，限以時日。

translations.literal: Those who wished to continue as before were to be registered on the market rolls by their local prefecture or county, their old inns torn down, and they were also to be sent far away, with a time limit set.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wished to stay in trade were registered on market rolls, their old inns demolished, and they were sent far away within a set time.

sentences.zh: 時逢冬塞，莫敢陳訴。

translations.literal: It was then deep winter and cold — no one dared to petition.
translations.idiomatic: It was deep winter; no one dared complain.

sentences.zh: 諤因別使，見其如此，以農工有業，各附所安，逆旅之與旗亭，自古非同一概，即附市籍，於理不可。

translations.literal: E, on a separate mission, saw how things stood and held that farmers and artisans each had their trades and each had where they belonged — inns and taverns had never been of one kind since antiquity; to attach them to market rolls was unreasonable in principle.
translations.idiomatic: On a separate mission E saw the hardship and argued that farmers and artisans each had their proper trade — inns and taverns had never been the same category since antiquity; registering them on market rolls was wrong in principle.

sentences.zh: 且行旅之所依託，豈容一朝而廢？

translations.literal: Moreover, how could what travelers rely upon be abolished in a single morning?
translations.idiomatic: And what travelers depend on — how could that be abolished overnight?

sentences.zh: 徒為勞擾，於事非宜。

translations.literal: It would only cause labor and disturbance, and was unsuitable in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: It would only bring turmoil, and served no good purpose.

sentences.zh: 遂專決之，並令依舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon he decided the matter on his own authority and ordered all to continue as before.
translations.idiomatic: He decided on his own authority and ordered all to continue as before.

sentences.zh: 使還詣闕，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned to court, only then did he report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Only after returning to court did he report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 文帝善之曰：「體國之臣，當如此矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen approved and said: "A minister who upholds the state should be like this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen praised him: "A minister who serves the realm should act as you have.

sentences.zh: 」以年老，出拜通州刺史，甚有惠政，人夷悅服。

translations.literal: " Because of his advanced age, he was sent out as Prefect of Tongzhou, where he governed with great benevolence and both Chinese and barbarians submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: " In his old age he was made Prefect of Tongzhou, where his benevolent rule won the glad submission of Chinese and barbarians alike.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 四子。

translations.literal: Four sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons.

sentences.zh: 世子大方襲爵，最有才器。

translations.literal: The eldest son Dafang inherited the title and was the most talented and capable.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Dafang inherited the title and was the most gifted.

sentences.zh: 大業初，判內史舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, he served as Acting Master of Documents in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daye reign he served as Acting Master of Documents in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 次大體、大鈞，並位尚書郎。

translations.literal: Next came Dati and Dajun, both of whom held posts as Directors in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Dati and Dajun, both of whom served as Directors in the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 鮑宏，字潤身，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Bao Hong, courtesy name Runshen, was a native of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Hong, styled Runshen, came from Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 父機，以才學知名。

translations.literal: His father Ji was known for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao Ji was known for talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，位書侍御史。

translations.literal: He served in Liang as Palace Secretary and Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he served as Palace Secretary and Censor.

sentences.zh: 宏七歲而孤，為兄泉之所愛育。

translations.literal: Hong was orphaned at seven and was lovingly raised by his elder brother Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Hong lost his father at seven and was lovingly raised by his elder brother Quan.

sentences.zh: 年十二，能屬文，嘗和湘東王繹詩，繹嗟賞不已，引為中記室。

translations.literal: At twelve he could compose literary pieces; once he matched a poem of Prince Yi of Xiangdong, and Yi sighed in admiration without end and took him on as Central Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he could write; he once matched a poem of Prince Yi of Xiangdong, who admired him endlessly and made him Central Recorder.

sentences.zh: 累遷通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Regular Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，歸於周，明帝甚禮之，引為麟趾殿學士。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he submitted to Zhou; Emperor Ming treated him with great ceremony and took him on as an Academician of Linzhi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell he went over to Zhou; Emperor Ming honored him and made him an Academician of Linzhi Hall.

sentences.zh: 累遷遂伯下大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Suibo.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Master of Suibo.

sentences.zh: 與杜子暉聘陳，謀伐齊，陳遂出兵度江以侵齊。

translations.literal: Together with Du Zihui he went on mission to Chen to plan an attack on Qi; Chen thereupon sent troops across the river to invade Qi.
translations.idiomatic: With Du Zihui he went on mission to Chen to plan war on Qi; Chen then sent troops across the Yangtze to strike Qi.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問巨集取齊策，巨集以為「先皇往日，出師洛陽，彼有其備，每不克捷。

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Hong for a strategy to take Qi; Hong said: "In former days when the late emperor marched on Luoyang, the enemy was prepared and each time we could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Hong how to take Qi; Hong said, "When the late emperor marched on Luoyang, Qi was ready each time and we could not win.

sentences.zh: 如臣計者，進兵汾、潞，直掩晉陽，出其不虞，以為上策。

translations.literal: According to my plan, advance on Fen and Lu, strike straight at Jinyang, catch them unawares — I take this as the upper strategy.
translations.idiomatic: By my plan, advance through Fen and Lu, strike Jinyang directly, catch them unaware — that is the best course.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 及定山東，除小禦正，賜爵平遙縣伯，加儀同。

translations.literal: When Shandong was pacified, he was appointed Junior Director of the Imperial Household and enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyao, with the additional rank of Commissioner with Distinction.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong was pacified he became Junior Director of the Imperial Household, was made Baron of Pingyao, and given the rank of Commissioner with Distinction.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝作相，奉使山南。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui became Chancellor, Hong went on mission to the south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui became Chancellor, Hong went on mission south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 會王謙舉兵于蜀，路次潼州，為謙將達奚惎所執，逼送成都，竟不屈節。

translations.literal: Wang Qian raised troops in Shu; on the road at Tongzhou he was seized by Qian's general Daxi Ji, forced to Chengdu, and in the end did not yield his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian rebelled in Shu; at Tongzhou on the road Hong was seized by Qian's general Daxi Ji, forced to Chengdu, and never broke.

sentences.zh: 謙敗，馳傳入京，文帝嘉之，賜以金帶。

translations.literal: When Qian was defeated, Hong rode post-horses to the capital; Emperor Wen praised him and granted a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian fell, Hong rode post-horses to the capital; Emperor Wen praised him and gave him a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，加開府，進爵為公。

translations.literal: After the accession, he was given the rank of Opening the Office and promoted to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: After the founding he was given Opening the Office and raised to Duke.

sentences.zh: 曆利、邛二州刺史，秩滿還京。

translations.literal: He successively served as Prefect of Li and Qiong; when his term expired he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Prefect of Li and Qiong in turn; when his terms ended he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時有尉義臣者，其父崇不從尉遲迥，從復與突厥戰死。

translations.literal: At that time there was Wei Yichen — his father Chong had not followed Yuwen Jiong, and Cong again died fighting the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was Wei Yichen — his father Chong had refused to follow Yuwen Jiong, and Cong had died fighting the Turks.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，將賜姓金氏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and was about to grant him the surname Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and was about to grant him the surname Jin.

sentences.zh: 訪及群下，宏曰：「昔項伯不同項羽，漢高賜其姓劉氏，秦真父能死難，魏武賜姓曹氏。

translations.literal: Consulting the assembled officials, Hong said: "In former times Xiang Bo did not follow Xiang Yu — Emperor Gao of Han granted him the surname Liu; Qin Zhenfu could die for the cause — Emperor Wu of Wei granted him the surname Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting his ministers, Hong said, "Xiang Bo refused to follow Xiang Yu, and Emperor Gao of Han gave him the Liu surname; Qin Zhenfu died for his lord, and Emperor Wu of Wei gave him the Cao surname.

sentences.zh: 請賜以皇族。

translations.literal: I ask that he be granted the imperial clan surname.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him the imperial surname.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Well said.

sentences.zh: 」因賜義臣姓楊。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yichen was granted the surname Yang.
translations.idiomatic: " Yichen was given the surname Yang.

sentences.zh: 後授均州刺史，以目疾免，卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Prefect of Jun, was dismissed for eye disease, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Prefect of Jun, was dismissed for eye disease, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 初，周武帝敕宏修《皇室譜》一部，分為《帝緒》、《疏屬》、《賜姓》三篇。

translations.literal: Initially, Emperor Wu of Zhou ordered Hong to compile a Royal Clan Genealogy in one work, divided into three sections: Imperial Lineage, Distant Kin, and Granted Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wu of Zhou had ordered Hong to compile a Royal Clan Genealogy in three parts: Imperial Lineage, Distant Kin, and Granted Surnames.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten fascicles, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in ten fascicles, which circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 高構，字孝基，北海人也。

translations.literal: Gao Gou, courtesy name Xiaoji, was a native of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gou, styled Xiaoji, came from Beihai.

sentences.zh: 性滑稽多智，辯給過人，好讀書，工吏事。

translations.literal: By nature witty and resourceful, more eloquent than others, fond of reading, and skilled in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was witty and clever, surpassingly eloquent, fond of books, and skilled in administration.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，曆蘭陵、平原二郡太守。

translations.literal: He served in Qi, successively as Prefect of Lanling and Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as Prefect of Lanling and Pingyuan in turn.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，周武帝以為許州司馬。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou made him Prefectural Secretary of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou made him Prefectural Secretary of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，累遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the Mandate, Gou was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Gou rose to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時內史侍郎晉平東與兄子長茂爭嫡，尚書省不以斷，朝臣三議不決。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director of the Secretariat Jin Pingdong and his elder brother's son Changmao disputed succession rights; the Ministry of State Affairs could not decide, and after three deliberations by court ministers there was still no resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Jin Pingdong and his nephew Changmao disputed who was the legitimate heir; the Ministry could not decide, and three rounds of court debate failed to settle it.

sentences.zh: 構斷而合理，上以為能，召入內殿，勞之曰：「我聞尚書郎上應列宿，觀卿才識，方知古人之言信矣。

translations.literal: Gou judged the case and his reasoning was sound; the emperor, thinking him capable, summoned him to the inner hall and commended him: "I have heard that Attendants of the Ministry correspond to the constellations — seeing your talent and judgment, I now know the words of the ancients were true.
translations.idiomatic: Gou decided the case soundly; the emperor, impressed, summoned him to the inner hall and said, "They say Ministry Attendants match the stars — your talent proves the ancients right.

sentences.zh: 嫡庶者，禮教之所重，我讀卿判數遍，詞理愜當，意所不能及也。

translations.literal: Legitimate and secondary sons — ritual teaching holds them weighty; I have read your judgment several times — the words and principle are satisfying and appropriate, beyond what I myself could reach.
translations.idiomatic: Legitimate and secondary succession is what ritual weighs most heavily; I have read your judgment again and again — its logic satisfies me beyond my own reach.

sentences.zh: 」賜米百石。

translations.literal: " He was granted a hundred shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: " He was rewarded with a hundred shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 由是知名。

translations.literal: From this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: From this he became famous.

sentences.zh: 馮翊武鄉女子焦氏既瘂又聾，嫁之不售。

translations.literal: In Wuxiang of Fufeng Commandery there was a woman surnamed Jiao who was both mute and deaf — no marriage could be arranged for her.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuxiang, Fufeng, a woman named Jiao was mute and deaf — no one would marry her.

sentences.zh: 嘗樵菜于野，為人所犯而有孕，遂生一男。

translations.literal: Once while gathering firewood and vegetables in the wild she was violated by a man and became pregnant, and bore a boy.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering firewood in the wild, she was assaulted and became pregnant, bearing a son.

sentences.zh: 時年六歲，莫知其姓，於是申省。

translations.literal: When the boy was six, no one knew his surname, and the matter was reported to the provincial office.
translations.idiomatic: At six the boy had no surname; the case went to the provincial office.

sentences.zh: 構判曰：「母不能言，窮究理絕。

translations.literal: Gou's judgment read: "The mother cannot speak — thorough investigation of principle reaches its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Gou ruled: "The mother cannot speak — inquiry reaches its limit.

sentences.zh: 案《風俗通》，姓有九種，或氏於爵，或氏所居。

translations.literal: According to the Customs and Commonplaces, there are nine kinds of surname — some from rank, some from place of residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Customs and Commonplaces lists nine kinds of surname — some from rank, some from place.

sentences.zh: 此兒生在武鄉，可以武為姓。

translations.literal: This child was born in Wuxiang — he may take Wu as his surname.
translations.idiomatic: This child was born in Wuxiang — let his surname be Wu.

sentences.zh: 」尋遷雍州司馬，以明斷見稱。

translations.literal: " Soon he was transferred to Prefectural Secretary of Yongzhou and was praised for clear judgment.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he became Prefectural Secretary of Yongzhou, praised for clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉吏部侍郎，號為稱職。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and was called competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became Vice Director of Personnel and was called competent.

sentences.zh: 復徙雍州司馬，坐事左轉盩厔令，甚有能名。

translations.literal: He was again moved to Prefectural Secretary of Yongzhou, was demoted for an offense to Magistrate of Zhouzhi, and was highly praised for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Yongzhou as Prefectural Secretary, was demoted to Magistrate of Zhouzhi for an offense, and won high praise for ability.

sentences.zh: 上善之，復拜雍州司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and again appointed him Prefectural Secretary of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and restored him as Prefectural Secretary of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，又為吏部侍郎，以公事免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he again became Vice Director of Personnel and was dismissed for a public matter.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Renshou he again became Vice Director of Personnel and was dismissed for an official matter.

sentences.zh: 煬帝立，召令復位。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended, he was summoned and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Gou was summoned back to office.

sentences.zh: 時為吏部者多以不稱去職，唯構最有能名，前後典選之官，皆出其下，時人以構好劇談，頗謂輕薄，然其內懷方雅，特為吏部尚書牛弘所重。

translations.literal: At that time most who served in Personnel were dismissed as incompetent — only Gou had the greatest reputation for ability; the officials who had previously managed selection all ranked below him. People of the time, because Gou loved sharp talk, largely called him frivolous — yet inwardly he held square elegance and was especially valued by Minister of Personnel Niu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Most Personnel directors of that era failed and were removed — only Gou was most famed for competence; every prior selection chief ranked below him. Men called him frivolous for his sharp tongue, yet inwardly he was upright and elegant, and Niu Hong especially valued him.

sentences.zh: 後以老病解職，弘時典選，凡將有所擢用，輒遣人就第問其可不。

translations.literal: Later, because of old age and illness he resigned; when Hong then managed selection, whenever he was about to promote someone he always sent a man to Gou's house to ask whether it was suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Later illness forced his retirement; when Hong managed selection, he always sent someone to Gou's home to ask whether a candidate was fit.

sentences.zh: 河東薛道衡才高當世，每稱構有清鑒，所為文筆，必先以草呈觀構而後出之。

translations.literal: Xue Daohang of Hedong, whose talent towered over his age, always said Gou had clear judgment — whatever literary work he wrote, he first sent a draft to Gou for review before releasing it.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daohang of Hedong, the age's greatest talent, said Gou had clear judgment — he always sent drafts to Gou before publishing his writing.

sentences.zh: 構有所詆訶，道衡未嘗不嗟伏。

translations.literal: Whenever Gou criticized something, Daohang never failed to sigh and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gou criticized his work, Daohang sighed and accepted.

sentences.zh: 大業七年，終於家。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daye he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye 7 he died at home.

sentences.zh: 所舉薦杜如晦、房玄齡等，後皆自致公輔，論者稱構有知人之鑒。

translations.literal: Those he recommended — Du Ruhui, Fang Xuanling, and others — later all reached the highest offices themselves; commentators said Gou had the eye to know men.
translations.idiomatic: Those he recommended — Du Ruhui, Fang Xuanling, and others — all rose to the highest offices; men said Gou could truly judge talent.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，昌黎豆盧實為黃門會郎，稱為慎密。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era, Dou Lushi of Changli served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate and was called careful and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang, Dou Lushi of Changli served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate and was called careful and thorough.

sentences.zh: 河東裴術為右丞，多所糾正。

translations.literal: Pei Shu of Hedong served as Right Vice Director and corrected many abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu of Hedong served as Right Vice Director and corrected many abuses.

sentences.zh: 河內士燮、平原東方舉、安定皇甫聿道，俱為刑部，並執法平允。

translations.literal: Shi Xie of Henei, Dongfang Ju of Pingyuan, and Huangfu Yudao of Anding all served in the Ministry of Punishments and equally upheld the law with fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xie of Henei, Dongfang Ju of Pingyuan, and Huangfu Yudao of Anding all served in Punishments and upheld the law with equal fairness.

sentences.zh: 京兆韋焜為戶部郎，屢進讜言。

translations.literal: Wei Kun of Jingzhao served as Director in the Ministry of Revenue and repeatedly offered straight remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Kun of Jingzhao served as Director in Revenue and repeatedly offered blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 南陽韓則為延州，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: Han Ze of Nanyang served as Prefect of Yanzhou and governed with great benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ze of Nanyang served as Prefect of Yanzhou with great benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 此等事行遺闕，皆有吏幹，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: These men's deeds and omissions in office all showed administrative ability and were praised in their time.
translations.idiomatic: These men's conduct in office, though imperfect, showed real administrative skill and won praise in their day.

sentences.zh: 榮毗，字子諶，北平無終人也。

translations.literal: Rong Pi, courtesy name Zichen, was a native of Wuzhong in Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Pi, styled Zichen, came from Wuzhong in Beiping.

sentences.zh: 父權，魏兵部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Quan was Minister of War of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rong Quan served as Minister of War under Wei.

sentences.zh: 毗少剛鯁，有局量，涉獵群言。

translations.literal: From youth Pi was firm and upright, had breadth of capacity, and ranged widely through many texts.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was upright and resolute from youth, broad in outlook, and widely read.

sentences.zh: 仕周，位內史下士。

translations.literal: He served in Zhou as Clerk in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he served as Clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，累遷殿內局監。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was repeatedly promoted to Supervisor of the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui's Kaihuang era he rose to Supervisor of the Palace Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時以華陰多盜賊，妙選長史，楊素薦毗為華州長史，世號為能。

translations.literal: At that time because Huayin had many bandits and thieves, a chief secretary was carefully chosen — Yang Su recommended Pi as Chief Secretary of Huazhou, and the age called him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Huayin was rife with bandits; Yang Su recommended Pi as Chief Secretary of Huazhou — and the age called him able.

sentences.zh: 素之田宅，多在華陰，左右放縱，毗以法繩之，無所寬貸。

translations.literal: Su's fields and houses were mostly in Huayin; his retainers were unrestrained, but Pi bound them with the law and showed no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Su owned much land in Huayin; his men ran wild, but Pi held them to the law without mercy.

sentences.zh: 毗因朝集，素謂之曰：「素之舉卿，適以自罰也？

translations.literal: At an assembly Pi said to him: "Did Su recommend you only to punish himself?
translations.idiomatic: At court assembly Su said to him, "Did I recommend you just to punish myself?

sentences.zh: 」毗答曰：「奉法一心者，但恐累公所舉。

translations.literal: " Pi replied: "One who upholds the law with single-mindedness — I only fear I may bring disgrace on what you recommended.
translations.idiomatic: " Pi answered, "I serve the law with all my heart — I only fear I may disgrace your recommendation.

sentences.zh: 」素笑曰：「前言戲耳。

translations.literal: " Su laughed and said: "What I said before was in jest.
translations.idiomatic: " Su laughed: "That was a joke.

sentences.zh: 卿之奉法，素之望也。

translations.literal: Your upholding the law is what Su hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Your fidelity to the law is exactly what I wanted.

sentences.zh: 」時晉王在揚州，每令人密覘京師消息，遣張衡于路次往往置馬坊，以畜牧為辭，實給私人也。

translations.literal: " At that time the Prince of Jin was in Yangzhou and often sent men secretly to observe news from the capital; he dispatched Zhang Heng to set up horse farms along the road, using livestock as pretext but in fact supplying private interests.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Jin was then in Yangzhou, sending men to spy on the capital; Zhang Heng set up horse farms along the roads — nominally for breeding, in fact for private supply.

sentences.zh: 州縣莫敢違，毗獨遏絕其事。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties dared not disobey — only Pi blocked and cut off the affair.
translations.idiomatic: No prefecture or county dared refuse — only Pi stopped it.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，賚絹百匹，轉蒲州司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and approved, granted a hundred bolts of silk, and transferred him to Prefectural Secretary of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and praised him, gave a hundred bolts of silk, and made him Prefectural Secretary of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒之反也，河東豪傑以城應諒。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, the magnates of Hedong opened the city to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, Hedong's powerful families surrendered the city to him.

sentences.zh: 刺史丘和覺變，遁歸關中。

translations.literal: Prefect Qiu He sensed the change and fled back to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Qiu He sensed trouble and fled to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 長史渤海高義明謂毗曰：「河東國之東門，若失之，則為難不細。

translations.literal: Chief Secretary Gao Yiming of Bohai said to Pi: "Hedong is the eastern gate of the state — if we lose it, the difficulty will not be small.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretary Gao Yiming of Bohai told Pi, "Hedong is the realm's eastern gate — lose it, and the damage is grave.

sentences.zh: 在中雖復匈匈，非悉反也。

translations.literal: Though there is turmoil within, not all have rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The turmoil within does not mean everyone has turned.

sentences.zh: 但收桀黠者十餘人斬之，自當立定耳。

translations.literal: Just seize and behead a dozen or so ringleaders — stability will follow of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Seize and behead a dozen ringleaders — order will restore itself.

sentences.zh: 」毗然之。

translations.literal: " Pi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Pi agreed.

sentences.zh: 義明馳馬追和，將與協計。

translations.literal: Yiming rode post-horses to overtake He and planned to coordinate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yiming rode after He to coordinate plans.

sentences.zh: 至城西門，為渤海所殺，毗亦被執。

translations.literal: At the west gate of the city he was killed by men of Bohai; Pi was also seized.
translations.idiomatic: At the west gate Yiming was killed by Bohai men; Pi was seized as well.

sentences.zh: 及諒平，拜書侍御史，帝謂曰：「今日之舉，馬坊之事也。

translations.literal: When Liang was pacified, Pi was appointed Palace Secretary and Censor; the emperor said: "Today's promotion is for the matter of the horse farms.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell, Pi became Palace Secretary and Censor; the emperor said, "This promotion is for the horse-farm affair.

sentences.zh: 無改汝心。

translations.literal: Do not change your heart.
translations.idiomatic: Do not change your heart.

sentences.zh: 」帝亦敬之。

translations.literal: " The emperor also respected him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor respected him as well.

sentences.zh: 毗在朝侃然正色，為百僚所憚。

translations.literal: Pi in court was stern and upright in countenance, and the hundred officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In court Pi was stern and upright, and officials feared him.

sentences.zh: 後以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Later he left office for mourning his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Later he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起令視事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was recalled to duty.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 毗兄建緒，性甚亮直，兼有學業。

translations.literal: Pi's elder brother Jianxu was by nature very bright and upright and also possessed learning.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's elder brother Jianxu was bright, upright, and learned.

sentences.zh: 仕周，為載師下大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He served in Zhou as Grand Master of the Transport Office and Third Rank Commissioner with Distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he was Grand Master of the Transport Office and Third Rank Commissioner with Distinction.

sentences.zh: 及平齊之始，留鎮鄴城，因著《齊紀》三十卷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the pacification of Qi he remained to garrison Ye and there wrote the Qi Chronicle in thirty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was first conquered he stayed to garrison Ye and wrote the Qi Chronicle in thirty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 建緒與文帝有舊，及為丞相，加位開府，拜息州刺史。

translations.literal: Jianxu had old ties with Emperor Wen; when Wen became Chancellor, he added the rank of Opening the Office and appointed him Prefect of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Jianxu was old friends with Emperor Wen; when Wen became Chancellor he gave him Opening the Office and made him Prefect of Xi.

sentences.zh: 將之官，時帝陰有禪代之計，因謂建緒曰：「且躊躇，當共取富貴耳。

translations.literal: As he was about to take office, the emperor secretly had a plan to receive the abdication and therefore said to Jianxu: "Hesitate a while — we shall together gain wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: As Jianxu prepared to leave, the emperor, planning abdication, said, "Wait — we shall share wealth and glory together.

sentences.zh: 」建緒自以周之大夫，因義形於色曰：「明公此旨，非僕所聞。

translations.literal: " Jianxu, taking himself as a grandee of Zhou, showed righteousness in his expression and said: "Your intent, my lord — this is not what your servant has heard.
translations.idiomatic: " Jianxu, a Zhou grandee, showed outrage: "My lord, such words I have never heard.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 建緒遂行。

translations.literal: Jianxu thereupon departed.
translations.idiomatic: Jianxu departed.

sentences.zh: 開皇初來朝，上謂之曰：「卿亦悔不？

translations.literal: In early Kaihuang he came to court; the emperor said to him: "Do you also regret it?
translations.idiomatic: In early Kaihuang he came to court; the emperor asked, "Do you regret it now?

sentences.zh: 」建緒稽首曰：「臣位非徐廣，情類楊彪。

translations.literal: " Jianxu bowed and said: "Your servant's rank is not that of Xu Guang — my sentiment is like that of Yang Biao.
translations.idiomatic: " Jianxu bowed: "I am no Xu Guang — my heart is Yang Biao's.

sentences.zh: 」上笑曰：「朕雖不解書語，亦知卿此言不遜也。

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed and said: "Though I do not understand book language, I also know your words are not modest.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed: "I may not know the classics, but I know impudence when I hear it.

sentences.zh: 」兼始、洪二州刺史，俱有能名。

translations.literal: " He also served as Prefect of Shi and Hong — both posts won him a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: " He served as Prefect of Shi and Hong, both with a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 陸知命，字仲通，吳郡富春人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhiming, courtesy name Zhongtong, was a native of Fuchun in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhiming, styled Zhongtong, came from Fuchun in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父敖，陳散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His father Ao was Attendant Cavalier of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lu Ao was Attendant Cavalier under Chen.

sentences.zh: 知命性好學，通識大體，以貞介自持。

translations.literal: Zhiming was fond of learning by nature, understood the larger pattern, and held himself with integrity and firmness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiming loved learning, grasped the larger pattern, and held himself with upright integrity.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，為太學博士、南獄正。

translations.literal: He served in Chen as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Corrector of the Southern Prison.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen he was Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Corrector of the Southern Prison.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，歸於家。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he went home.

sentences.zh: 會高智慧等作亂于江左，晉王廣鎮江都，以其三吳之望召令諷諭反者。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhihui and others raised rebellion in the Jiangzuo, Prince Guang of Jin was stationed at Jiangdu and, because of his standing in the Three Wu region, summoned him to admonish the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui rebelled in the lower Yangtze, Prince Guang of Jin, stationed at Jiangdu, summoned him — for his standing in the Three Wu — to persuade the rebels.

sentences.zh: 以功拜儀同三司，賜以田宅，復用其弟恪為汧陽令。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted Third Rank Commissioner with Distinction, given fields and houses, and his younger brother Ke was again appointed Magistrate of Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received Third Rank Commissioner with Distinction, fields and a house, and his brother Ke was made Magistrate of Qianyang.

sentences.zh: 知命以恪非百里才，上表陳讓，朝廷許之。

translations.literal: Zhiming held that Ke lacked the talent for a hundred-li district and submitted a memorial declining — the court permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiming held Ke unfit for a magistracy and memorialized to decline — the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 時見天下一統，知命詣朝堂上表，請使高麗以宣示皇風，使彼君臣面縛闕下。

translations.literal: When he saw the realm unified, Zhiming went to the court hall and submitted a memorial asking that an envoy be sent to Goguryeo to proclaim the imperial wind and bring their ruler and ministers bound before the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the realm unified, Zhiming memorialized from the court hall asking that an envoy go to Goguryeo to proclaim imperial virtue and bring their ruler bound to the palace steps.

sentences.zh: 書奏，天子異之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Son of Heaven was struck by it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by the memorial.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，授普寧鎮將。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Garrison General of Puning.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made Garrison General of Puning.

sentences.zh: 人或言其正直者。

translations.literal: Some spoke of his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Some praised his uprightness.

sentences.zh: 由是待詔于御史臺。

translations.literal: On this account he awaited edicts at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: On that account he awaited edicts at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜書侍御史，侃然正色，為百僚所憚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was appointed Palace Secretary and Censor — stern and upright in countenance, feared by the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded he became Palace Secretary and Censor — stern, upright, and feared by officials.

sentences.zh: 帝甚敬之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly respected him.

sentences.zh: 後坐事免。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復職。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was restored.

sentences.zh: 時齊王暕頗驕縱，昵近小人，知命奏劾之，暕竟得罪，百僚震栗。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Qi Yang was quite arrogant and unrestrained, intimate with petty men — Zhiming memorialized to impeach him; Yang was indeed punished, and the hundred officials trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Yang was arrogant and fond of petty men; Zhiming impeached him — Yang was punished, and officials trembled.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，為東暆道受降使者，卒于師。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he served as Surrender Envoy on the Dongyi Route and died on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he was Surrender Envoy on the Dongyi Route and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 贈御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 梁毗，字景和，安定烏氏人也。

translations.literal: Lian Pi, courtesy name Jinghe, was a native of Wushi in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Pi, styled Jinghe, came from Wushi in Anding.

sentences.zh: 祖越，魏涇、豫、洛三州刺史，郃陽縣公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yue was Prefect of Jing, Yu, and Luo in Wei and Duke of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lian Yue was Prefect of Jing, Yu, and Luo under Wei and Duke of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 父茂，周滄、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Mao was Prefect of Cang and Yan in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lian Mao was Prefect of Cang and Yan under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 毗性剛謇，頗有學涉。

translations.literal: Pi was by nature blunt and upright, and was quite learned.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was blunt and upright by nature, and well learned.

sentences.zh: 仕周，累遷布憲下大夫。

translations.literal: He served in Zhou and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Proclaiming the Law.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he rose to Grand Master of Proclaiming the Law.

sentences.zh: 宣政中，封易陽縣子，遷武藏大夫。

translations.literal: In the Xuanzheng era he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yiyang and transferred to Grand Master of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanzheng era he was made Viscount of Yiyang and transferred to Grand Master of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the Mandate, his rank was advanced to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Pi was raised to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，以鯁正，拜書侍御史，名為稱職。

translations.literal: In early Kaihuang, for blunt uprightness he was appointed Palace Secretary and Censor and was called competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kaihuang his blunt integrity won him Palace Secretary and Censor — and a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 轉大興令，遷雍州贊務。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Daxing and moved to Assistant Administrator of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became Magistrate of Daxing, then Assistant Administrator of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 毗既出憲司，復典京邑，直道而行，無所回避，頗失權貴心，由是出為西寧州刺史，改封邯鄲縣侯。

translations.literal: Pi, having left the Censorate, again governed the capital region — walking the straight path without evasion, he quite lost the hearts of the powerful; for this reason he was sent out as Prefect of Xining and his fief was changed to Marquis of Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the Censorate to govern the capital, Pi walked the straight path without flinching — and lost the powerful; he was sent out as Prefect of Xining and made Marquis of Handan.

sentences.zh: 在州十一年。

translations.literal: He was in the prefecture eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the prefecture eleven years.

sentences.zh: 先是，蠻夷酋長皆服金冠，以金多者為豪俊，由是遞相陵辱，每尋干戈，邊境略無寧歲。

translations.literal: Before this, barbarian chieftains all wore gold crowns — whoever had the most gold was considered bold and outstanding; on this account they successively insulted one another and constantly sought battle — the borderlands scarcely knew a year of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian chiefs had worn gold crowns — the most gold meant the greatest standing — and they fought endlessly; the frontier knew no peace.

sentences.zh: 毗患之，後因諸酋長相率以金遺之，於是置金座側，對之慟哭，謂曰：「此饑不可食，寒不可衣，汝等以此相滅。

translations.literal: Pi was troubled by this; later, when the chieftains in succession brought him gold as gifts, he placed the gold beside his seat and wept before them, saying: "This cannot be eaten when hungry, cannot be worn when cold — you use this to destroy one another.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was troubled; when chiefs brought him gold in succession, he set it beside his seat and wept: "This cannot feed hunger or clothe cold — yet you kill each other for it.

sentences.zh: 今將此來，欲殺我邪！

translations.literal: You bring this now — do you wish to kill me?
translations.idiomatic: Have you brought this to kill me?

sentences.zh: 」無所納，悉以還之。

translations.literal: " He accepted nothing and returned it all.
translations.idiomatic: " He accepted none and returned it all.

sentences.zh: 於是蠻夷感悟，遂不相攻。

translations.literal: Thereupon the barbarians were moved and no longer attacked one another.
