translations.idiomatic: The barbarians were moved and stopped fighting each other.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞而善之，徵為散騎常侍、大理卿。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen heard and approved, summoned him as Palace Attendant and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen heard and praised him, summoning him as Palace Attendant and Director of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 處法平允，時人稱之。

translations.literal: His application of the law was fair and even, and people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He applied the law fairly, and men praised him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，進位上開府。

translations.literal: After more than a year his rank was advanced to Upper Opening the Office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was given Upper Opening the Office.

sentences.zh: 毗見左僕射楊素貴重擅權，百僚震懾，恐為國患，因上封事曰：「竊見左僕射越國公素，幸遇愈重，權勢日隆，所私皆非忠讜，所進咸是親戚，子弟布州，兼州連縣。

translations.literal: Pi saw that Left Vice Director Yang Su of Yue was honored and heavy, monopolizing power — the hundred officials trembled in fear, and he feared he would become a calamity to the state; he therefore submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Your servant secretly observes that Left Vice Director Duke of Yue Su — the more favored he is, the daily his power and influence grow; those he favors are none loyal and straight, those he promotes are all kin; his sons and younger brothers fill prefectures, holding several prefectures and linking counties.
translations.idiomatic: Pi saw Left Vice Director Yang Su honored and powerful, feared a national calamity, and submitted a sealed memorial: "Left Vice Director Duke of Yue Su grows ever more favored and powerful; his favorites are never loyal counselors, his promotions are all kin; sons and brothers fill prefectures across linked counties.

sentences.zh: 天下無事，容息奸圖，四海稍虞，必為禍始。

translations.literal: While the realm is at peace, treacherous designs may rest — but if the four seas are slightly troubled, he will surely be the source of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In peace treachery may sleep — but let trouble stir, and he will be its source.

sentences.zh: 夫奸臣擅命，有漸而來。

translations.literal: Treacherous ministers who monopolize command come gradually.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous ministers who seize power come by degrees.

sentences.zh: 王莽資之於積年，桓玄基之于易世，而卒殄漢祀，終傾晉祚。

translations.literal: Wang Mang built on years of accumulation; Huan Xuan laid foundations in a changed age — yet in the end they extinguished Han's sacrifices and overturned Jin's throne.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang built over years; Huan Xuan over a changed age — yet both ended Han sacrifice and overturned Jin's throne.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以素為阿衡，臣恐其心未必伊尹也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty takes Su as your Yi Yin, your servant fears his heart is not necessarily Yi Yin's.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty treats Su as your Yi Yin, I fear his heart is not Yi Yin's.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，命有司禁止，親自詰之。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly enraged, ordered the responsible offices to restrain him, and personally interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor raged, ordered him restrained, and interrogated him personally.

sentences.zh: 毗極言曰：「素既擅權寵，作威作福，將領之處，殺戮無道。

translations.literal: Pi spoke with utmost force: "Su already monopolizes power and favor, makes might and makes blessing — wherever he leads troops, he kills without principle.
translations.idiomatic: Pi spoke bluntly: "Su already monopolizes power and favor, makes might and blessing — wherever he commands, he kills without justice.

sentences.zh: 又太子、蜀王罪廢之日，百僚無不震悚，唯素揚眉奮肘，喜見容色，利國家有事以為身幸。

translations.literal: Moreover on the days when the crown prince and Prince of Shu were condemned and deposed, the hundred officials were none but fearful — only Su raised his brows and flexed his elbows, delight showing on his face, treating trouble to the state as personal good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince and Prince of Shu were deposed, every official trembled — only Su raised his brows in delight, treating the state's trouble as his good fortune.

sentences.zh: 」毗發言謇謇，有誠亮之節，帝無以屈也，乃釋之。

translations.literal: " Pi spoke with blunt integrity and had the integrity of sincerity — the emperor could not bend him and thereupon released him.
translations.idiomatic: " Pi spoke with blunt integrity the emperor could not refute — and released him.

sentences.zh: 素自此恩寵漸衰。

translations.literal: From this Su's favor gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: From this Su's favor waned.

sentences.zh: 但素任寄隆重，多所折挫，當時朝士無不懾伏；

translations.literal: But Su's trust and commission were weighty — he suffered many setbacks; court gentlemen of the time were none but fearful and submissive;
translations.idiomatic: Su remained heavily entrusted and suffered many setbacks; courtiers all feared him;

sentences.zh: 有敢與相是非，辭氣不撓者，獨毗與柳彧及尚書左丞李綱而已。

translations.literal: Those who dared dispute with him without bending in tone — only Pi, Liu Yu, and Left Assistant Director Li Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Only Pi, Liu Yu, and Left Assistant Director Li Gang dared dispute him without bending.

sentences.zh: 後上不復專委于素，蓋由察毗之言。

translations.literal: Later the emperor no longer exclusively entrusted affairs to Su — largely because he observed Pi's words.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor no longer entrusted everything to Su — largely because of Pi's words.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷刑部尚書，並攝御史大夫事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended, Pi was transferred to Minister of Punishments and concurrently handled the affairs of Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Pi became Minister of Punishments and concurrently handled the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 奏劾宇文述和私役部兵，帝議免述罪，毗固爭，因忤旨，遂令張衡代為大夫。

translations.literal: He memorialized to impeach Yuwen Shu for privately employing troops from his department; the emperor considered pardoning Shu — Pi firmly contested and thereby offended the imperial will; he was thereupon replaced as Censor-in-Chief by Zhang Heng.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Yuwen Shu for privately employing departmental troops; the emperor meant to pardon Shu — Pi contested fiercely, offended the throne, and Zhang Heng replaced him as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 毗憂憤卒。

translations.literal: Pi died of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Pi died of grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 帝令吏部尚書牛弘吊之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Minister of Personnel Niu Hong to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Minister of Personnel Niu Hong to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 子敬真，位大理司直。

translations.literal: His son Jingzhen held the post of Directing Secretary in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingzhen served as Directing Secretary in Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 時煬帝欲成光祿大夫魚俱羅罪，令敬真案其獄，遂希旨陷之極刑。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Yang wished to complete the guilt of Palace Attendant Yu Jurong and ordered Jingzhen to try the case — he thereupon toed the imperial intent and framed him to the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang wished to convict Palace Attendant Yu Jurong and ordered Jingzhen to try the case — Jingzhen toed the imperial will and framed him to death.

sentences.zh: 未幾，敬真有疾，見俱羅為祟而死。

translations.literal: Before long Jingzhen fell ill, saw Jurong haunting him, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jingzhen fell ill, saw Jurong's ghost, and died.

sentences.zh: 柳彧，字幼文，河東人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yu, courtesy name Youwen, was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, styled Youwen, came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 世居襄陽。

translations.literal: His family had long resided in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 父仲禮，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Zhongli has a biography in the Nanshi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Zhongli has an entry in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 仲禮，梁敗見囚于周，復家河東。

translations.literal: Zhongli, when Liang was defeated, was taken prisoner by Zhou and his family was restored to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell, Zhongli was taken by Zhou; the family returned to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 彧少好學，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: From youth Yu was fond of learning and ranged quite widely through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Yu loved learning from youth and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為中外府記室，久而出為甯州總管掾。

translations.literal: Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu of Zhou took him on as Recorder of the Inner and Outer Offices; after a long time he went out as Staff Officer to the Inspector-General of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu took him as Recorder of the Inner and Outer Offices; later he became Staff Officer to the Inspector-General of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 武帝親總萬機，彧詣闕求試。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Yu went to the palace gate to request a trial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took personal charge of government, Yu petitioned at court for a trial appointment.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，以為司武中士。

translations.literal: The emperor was struck by him and appointed him Clerk in the Office of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and made him Clerk in the Office of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉鄭令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He became Magistrate of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 平齊之後，帝賞從官，留京者不預。

translations.literal: After Qi was pacified, the emperor rewarded followers — those who remained in the capital were not included.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi was pacified the emperor rewarded his followers — but not those who had stayed in the capital.

sentences.zh: 彧上表曰：「今太平告始，信賞宜明，酬勳報勞，務先有本。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a memorial saying: "Now peace is newly proclaimed — trust and reward should be clear; repaying merit and replying to labor should above all have a basis.
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized: "Peace is newly won — rewards must be clear; merit and toil deserve a foundation.

sentences.zh: 屠城破邑，出自聖規，斬將搴旗，必由神略。

translations.literal: Storming cities and breaking settlements issue from the sage plan; beheading generals and seizing banners must follow divine strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Storming cities and breaking settlements come from the sage plan; seizing banners and beheading generals follow divine strategy.

sentences.zh: 若負戈擐甲，征扞劬勞。

translations.literal: If one bears weapons and dons armor, campaigning and defending with toil and labor —
translations.idiomatic: If men bear arms and armor, campaigning and defending with toil —

sentences.zh: 至於鎮撫國家，宿衛為重。

translations.literal: As for pacifying and comforting the state, garrison duty is weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying the state and guarding the capital are equally weighty.

sentences.zh: 俱稟成算，非專己能，留從事同，功勞須等。

translations.literal: All alike received the completed plan — it was not solely one's own ability; those who remained and those who followed shared the same work — merit should be equal.
translations.idiomatic: All shared the same plan — no man acted alone; those who stayed and those who marched shared the work — merit should be equal.

sentences.zh: 」於是留守並加品級。

translations.literal: " Thereupon those who had remained were all given added rank.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who had remained were all given added rank.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，曆尚書虞部、屯田二侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the Mandate, Yu successively served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and the Ministry of Colonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Yu served as Vice Director of Works and of Colonies in turn.

sentences.zh: 時制三品已上，門皆列戟。

translations.literal: At that time the regulation was that for third rank and above, gates all displayed halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank officials and above were required to display halberds at their gates.

sentences.zh: 左僕射高熲子弘德封應國公，申牒請戟。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Gao Jiong's son Hongde was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying and submitted a petition requesting halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Gao Jiong's son Hongde, Duke of Ying, petitioned for gate halberds.

sentences.zh: 彧判曰：「僕射之子更不異居，父之戟槊已列門外，尊有厭卑之義，子有避父之禮，豈容外門既設，內閣又施？

translations.literal: Yu's judgment read: "The Vice Director's son does not live separately — his father's halberds and spears are already set outside the gate; the honored have the meaning of surfeiting the lowly, sons have the ritual of avoiding the father — how can the outer gate already be set and the inner hall also be furnished?
translations.idiomatic: Yu ruled: "The Vice Director's son lives with his father — halberds already stand at the gate; honor surfeits the lowly, sons avoid fathers — how can the outer gate bear halberds and the inner hall bear them too?

sentences.zh: 」事竟不行。

translations.literal: " The matter in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 熲聞而歎伏。

translations.literal: Jiong heard and sighed in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong heard and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 後遷書侍御史，當朝正色，甚為百僚敬憚。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Palace Secretary and Censor — upright in countenance at court, greatly feared and respected by the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Palace Secretary and Censor — upright at court, greatly feared and respected.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其婞直，謂曰：「大丈夫當立名於世，無容容而已。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his blunt uprightness and said: "A great man should establish his name in the world — he cannot merely be accommodating.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his blunt integrity: "A great man must make a name in the world — not merely accommodate.

sentences.zh: 」賜錢十萬，米百石。

translations.literal: " He was granted a hundred thousand coins and a hundred shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: " He was given a hundred thousand coins and a hundred shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 時刺史多任武將，類不稱職，彧上表曰：「伏見詔書以上柱國和幹子為杞州刺史，其人年垂八十。

translations.literal: At that time most prefects were military generals — for the most part incompetent — and Yu submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant observes that the edict appoints Upper Pillar of State He Ganzi as Prefect of Qi — that man is nearly eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Most prefects were military men and incompetent; Yu memorialized: "The edict makes Upper Pillar He Ganzi Prefect of Qi — he is nearly eighty.

sentences.zh: 鐘鳴漏盡。

translations.literal: The bell has sounded and the clepsydra is empty.
translations.idiomatic: His hour has come.

sentences.zh: 前在趙州，暗於職務，政由群小，賄賂公行。

translations.literal: Previously in Zhaozhou he was dark to his duties — governance was in the hands of petty men and bribes flowed openly.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhaozhou he was blind to duty — petty men ruled and bribes flowed openly.

sentences.zh: 百姓籲嗟，歌謠滿道，乃云：'老禾不早殺，余種穢良田。

translations.literal: The common people lamented — songs filled the roads — saying: "If the old grain is not cut down early, the remaining seed fouls the good field.
translations.idiomatic: The people lamented — songs filled the roads: "If the old stalk is not cut early, the seed fouls the good field.

sentences.zh: '古人云：'耕當問奴，織當問婢。

translations.literal: " The ancients said: "In plowing ask the slave, in weaving ask the maid.
translations.idiomatic: " The ancients said, "Ask the slave about plowing, the maid about weaving.

sentences.zh: '此言各有所能也。

translations.literal: " This saying means each has what he can do.
translations.idiomatic: " Each has his own skill.

sentences.zh: 幹子弓馬武用，是其所長；

translations.literal: Ganzi's bow, horse, and military use — these are what he is good at;
translations.idiomatic: Ganzi excels at bow, horse, and war;

sentences.zh: 臨人蒞職，非其所解。

translations.literal: Facing men and overseeing office — this he does not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Governing men and office he does not understand.

sentences.zh: 如謂優老尚年，自可厚賜金帛，若令刺舉，所損殊大。

translations.literal: If one says to honor the aged and respect years, one may thickly grant gold and silk — but if one makes him investigate and report, the harm is especially great.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to honor his age, give him gold and silk — but make him investigate and report, and the harm is great.

sentences.zh: 臣死而後已，敢不竭誠。

translations.literal: Your servant will not stop until death — how dare he not exhaust sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I will not stop until death — how can I fail to speak plainly?

sentences.zh: 」上善之，幹子竟免。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved; Ganzi was ultimately exempted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved; Ganzi was spared.

sentences.zh: 有應州刺史唐君明，居母喪，娶雍州長史厙狄士文之從父妹。

translations.literal: There was Prefect of Yingzhou Tang Junming — while in mourning for his mother he married the younger sister of Assistant Administrator of Yongzhou Qiu Di Shiwen's paternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Tang Junming of Yingzhou, while mourning his mother, married the younger sister of Assistant Administrator Qiu Di Shiwen's paternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 彧劾之曰：「君明忽劬勞之痛，惑嬿爾之親，冒此苴縗，命彼褕翟。

translations.literal: Yu impeached him saying: "Junming ignored the pain of toil and mourning, was deluded by intimate affection, donned this hemp mourning yet took that brocade and pheasant-feather dress.
translations.idiomatic: Yu impeached him: "Junming ignored mourning's pain, was led astray by intimacy, wore hemp mourning yet took brocade and pheasant dress.

sentences.zh: 不義不昵，《春秋》載其將亡：無禮無儀，詩人欲其遄死。

translations.literal: Without righteousness, without intimacy — the Spring and Autumn Annals records that such men are about to perish; without ritual, without propriety — the poets wish them a swift death.
translations.idiomatic: Without righteousness or intimacy — the Spring and Autumn Annals says such men are doomed; without ritual or propriety — the poets wish them dead.

sentences.zh: 士文贊務神州，名位通顯，棄二姓之重匹，違六禮之軌儀。

translations.literal: Shiwen assists in the divine region, his name and rank broadly displayed — he cast aside the weight of two surnames' proper match and violated the track of the Six Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwen serves the sacred realm, famous and high — yet cast aside proper marriage between two surnames and violated the Six Rites.

sentences.zh: 請禁錮終身，以懲風俗。

translations.literal: I ask that both be confined for life, to warn custom.
translations.idiomatic: Confine both for life, to warn custom.

sentences.zh: 」二家竟坐得罪。

translations.literal: " Both families were indeed punished for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: " Both families were punished.

sentences.zh: 隋承喪亂之後，風俗頹壞，彧多所矯正，上甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Sui inherited after the age of mourning and chaos — customs were in ruin; Yu corrected much, and the emperor greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: Sui rose after chaos — customs were ruined; Yu corrected much, and the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 又見上勤於聽受，百僚奏請多有煩碎，因上疏諫曰：「人君出令，誡在煩數。

translations.literal: He also saw that the emperor was diligent in listening and accepting — the hundred officials' memorials and requests were often trivial — and therefore submitted a remonstrance saying: "When the ruler of men issues orders, the warning lies in frequency.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor listened diligently but officials' memorials grew trivial; Yu remonstrated: "When a ruler issues orders, the danger is frequency.

sentences.zh: 是以舜任五臣，堯咨四嶽，設官分職，各有司存，垂拱無為，天下以乂。

translations.literal: Thus Shun employed five ministers, Yao consulted the Four Peaks, established offices and divided duties — each had his department; draped arms in idleness — the realm was governed.
translations.idiomatic: Shun employed five ministers, Yao consulted the Four Peaks, divided offices — each had his charge; arms draped, the realm was governed.

sentences.zh: 所謂勞於求賢，逸于任使。

translations.literal: This is what is called labor in seeking the worthy, ease in employing them.
translations.idiomatic: Labor in seeking talent, ease in employing it.

sentences.zh: 比見事無大小，咸關聖職。

translations.literal: Recently I see that matters great and small all touch the sage office.
translations.idiomatic: Lately matters great and small all reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 陛下留心政道，無憚疲勞，至乃營造細小之事，出給輕微之物，一日之內，酬答百司，至乃日旰忘食貧，分夜未寢，動以文簿，憂勞聖躬。

translations.literal: Your Majesty attends to governance without fearing fatigue — even to planning small constructions and issuing trivial objects; within a single day you reply to the hundred offices — even until the sun sets and you forget food, divide the night and still not sleep, moved by documents, worrying and laboring the sage person.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty attends to every detail without rest — even small constructions and trivial grants; within a day you answer a hundred offices — until sunset without food, until midnight without sleep, worn by documents.

sentences.zh: 伏願思臣至言，少減煩務。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly wishes Your Majesty to reflect on your servant's utmost words and slightly reduce trivial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed my words and lighten the burden of trivial affairs.

sentences.zh: 」上覽而嘉之。

translations.literal: " The emperor read and approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor read and praised it.

sentences.zh: 以其家，敕有司與之築宅，因曰：「柳彧正直之士，國之龜寶也。

translations.literal: Because of his household, he ordered the responsible offices to build a residence for him, saying: "Liu Yu is an upright man — a tortoise treasure of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a house built for Yu, saying, "Liu Yu is upright — a national treasure.

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: " This is how highly he was regarded.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem he won.

sentences.zh: 右僕射楊素當途顯貴，百僚懾憚，無敢忤者，嘗以少譴，敕送南台。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Yang Su was powerful and honored on the road — the hundred officials feared him, none dared oppose; once for a minor fault an edict sent him to the Southern Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Yang Su was powerful — officials feared him, none opposed; once for a minor fault an edict sent him to the Southern Censorate.

sentences.zh: 素恃貴，坐彧床。

translations.literal: Su relied on his honor and sat on Yu's couch.
translations.idiomatic: Su, relying on rank, sat on Yu's couch.

sentences.zh: 彧從外來，見素如此，於階下端笏整容曰：「奉敕推公罪。

translations.literal: Yu came from outside, saw Su thus, and at the foot of the steps held his tablet and composed his countenance, saying: "By edict I am to investigate your lordship's offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yu entered, saw Su sitting there, and at the steps straightened his tablet: "By edict I investigate your offense.

sentences.zh: 」素遽下。

translations.literal: " Su hastily descended.
translations.idiomatic: " Su hurried down.

sentences.zh: 彧據案坐，立素於庭前，辯詰事狀。

translations.literal: Yu sat at the desk, made Su stand in the courtyard, and examined and questioned the facts of the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sat at his desk, made Su stand in the courtyard, and examined the case.

sentences.zh: 素由是銜之。

translations.literal: Su on this account harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Su nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 彧時方為上所信任，故素未有以中之。

translations.literal: Yu was then trusted by the emperor — therefore Su had no means to strike at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was then trusted by the emperor — Su could not strike at him.

sentences.zh: 彧見近代以來，都邑百姓每至正月十五日，作角抵戲，遞相誇競，至於糜費財力，上奏請禁絕之曰：「竊見京邑，爰及外州，每以正月望夜，充街塞陌，鳴鼓聒天，燎炬照地，人戴獸面，男為女服，倡優雜伎，詭狀異形。

translations.literal: Yu saw that in recent times, capital residents every year on the fifteenth day of the first month performed horn-butting games, successively boasting and competing, even to wasting and exhausting wealth and strength — he submitted a memorial asking that it be forbidden, saying: "Your servant secretly observes that the capital city, reaching also to outer prefectures, every year on the night of the full moon of the first month fills streets and blocks — drums thunder to the sky, torches light the ground; people wear beast masks, men dress as women, actors and mixed performers — bizarre forms and strange shapes.
translations.idiomatic: Yu saw that every Lantern Festival capital residents performed wrestling games, wasting wealth — and memorialized to ban it: "Every full moon of the first month fills streets — drums thunder, torches blaze; beast masks, men in women's dress, actors in bizarre shapes.

sentences.zh: 外內共觀，曾不相避。

translations.literal: Inside and outside together watch — never avoiding one another.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside watch together without restraint.

sentences.zh: 竭貲破產，競此一時。

translations.literal: Exhausting wealth and breaking estates — all compete for this one moment.
translations.idiomatic: Men exhaust wealth competing for this one night.

sentences.zh: 盡室並孥，無問貴賤，男女混雜，緇素不分。

translations.literal: Whole households with dependents — regardless of noble or base — men and women mixed, black and white undistinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Whole households turn out — noble and base, men and women mixed, lay and clerical undistinguished.

sentences.zh: 穢行因此而生，盜賊由斯而起。

translations.literal: Filthy conduct thereby arises; bandits and thieves thereby begin.
translations.idiomatic: Filthy conduct arises; theft follows.

sentences.zh: 非益於化，實損於人。

translations.literal: It does not benefit transformation — it truly harms men.
translations.idiomatic: It benefits no one — it harms all.

sentences.zh: 請頒天下，並即禁斷。

translations.literal: I ask that it be promulgated throughout the realm and immediately forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Ban it throughout the realm at once.

sentences.zh: 」詔可其奏。

translations.literal: " An edict approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 是歲，持節巡河北五十二州，奏免長吏贓汙不稱職者二百餘人，州縣肅然，莫不震懼。

translations.literal: That year, bearing the staff of authority he inspected fifty-two prefectures of Hebei and memorialized dismissal of more than two hundred chief officials who were corrupt and incompetent — prefectures and counties were stern, all fearing and awed.
translations.idiomatic: That year he inspected fifty-two Hebei prefectures and dismissed more than two hundred corrupt officials — prefectures and counties trembled.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，賜絹布二百匹，氈三十領，拜儀同三司，歲餘，加員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, granted two hundred bolts of silk and cloth and thirty felts, appointed him Third Rank Commissioner with Distinction, and after more than a year added Supernumerary Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, gave two hundred bolts of silk and thirty felts, made him Third Rank Commissioner with Distinction, and a year later Supernumerary Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，持節巡省太原道十九州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou, bearing the staff he inspected and toured nineteen prefectures of the Taiyuan Route.
translations.idiomatic: At Renshou's start he inspected nineteen prefectures on the Taiyuan Route.

sentences.zh: 及還，賜絹百五十匹。

translations.literal: When he returned he was granted a hundred fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: On return he received a hundred fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 彧嘗得博陵李文博所撰《政道集》十卷，蜀王秀遣人求之。

translations.literal: Yu once obtained the Collected Writings on Governance in ten fascicles by Li Wenbo of Boling — Prince of Shu Xiu sent a man to request it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu obtained Li Wenbo of Boling's Collected Writings on Governance in ten fascicles — Prince of Shu Xiu sent to request it.

sentences.zh: 彧送之於秀，秀復賜彧奴婢十口。

translations.literal: Yu sent it to Xiu; Xiu in return granted Yu ten slaves and maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent it to Xiu; Xiu gave him ten slaves and maidservants in return.

sentences.zh: 及秀得罪，楊素奏彧以內臣交通諸侯，除名，配戍懷遠鎮。

translations.literal: When Xiu was condemned, Yang Su memorialized that Yu, as an inner court official, had dealings with feudal lords — his name was removed and he was assigned to garrison Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu fell, Su memorialized that Yu, an inner official, had dealings with princes — Yu was struck from the rolls and sent to garrison Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 行達高陽，有詔徵進。

translations.literal: On the road reaching Gaoyang, an edict summoned him to advance.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoyang an edict summoned him forward.

sentences.zh: 至晉陽，遇漢王諒作亂，遣使馳召彧入城。

translations.literal: Reaching Jinyang, he encountered Prince of Han Liang's rebellion — an envoy was dispatched post-haste to summon Yu into the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang he met Prince Han Liang's rebellion — an envoy summoned him into the city.

sentences.zh: 而諒反形已露，彧入城，度不得免，遂詐中惡不食，自稱危篤。

translations.literal: But Liang's rebellious form was already exposed; Yu entered the city, judged he could not escape, and therefore feigned sudden illness, refusing food, calling himself critically ill.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's rebellion was already plain; Yu entered the city, knew he could not escape, feigned sudden illness, refused food, and called himself dying.

sentences.zh: 諒怒囚之。

translations.literal: Liang was enraged and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang imprisoned him in rage.

sentences.zh: 及諒敗，楊素奏彧心懷兩端，以候事變，跡雖不反，心實同逆。

translations.literal: When Liang was defeated, Yang Su memorialized that Yu harbored two minds, waiting for events to change — though his tracks did not rebel, his heart was truly the same as rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell, Su memorialized that Yu waited on events with divided loyalty — though he did not rebel openly, his heart was treasonous.

sentences.zh: 坐徙敦煌。

translations.literal: He was punished by exile to Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 素卒，乃自申理，有詔徵還。

translations.literal: When Su died, Yu then appealed on his own behalf — an edict summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Su died, Yu appealed — an edict summoned him back.

sentences.zh: 卒於道。

translations.literal: He died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the road.

sentences.zh: 有子紹，為介休令。

translations.literal: He had a son Shao, who was Magistrate of Jiexiu.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Shao, Magistrate of Jiexiu.

sentences.zh: 趙綽，字士倬，河東人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Chao, courtesy name Shizhuo, was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chao, styled Shizhuo, came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 性質直剛毅。

translations.literal: By nature he was straightforward, upright, and firm.
translations.idiomatic: He was straightforward, upright, and firm by nature.

sentences.zh: 周初為天官府史，以恭謹恪勤，擢授夏官府下士。

translations.literal: In early Zhou he was a clerk in the Heavenly Office; for respectful care and diligent effort he was promoted to Clerk in the Summer Office.
translations.idiomatic: In early Zhou he was a clerk in the Heavenly Office; for diligence and care he rose to Clerk in the Summer Office.

sentences.zh: 稍以明幹見知，為內史中士。

translations.literal: Gradually for clarity and competence he was known and made Clerk in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For clarity and competence he became Secretariat Clerk.

sentences.zh: 父艱去職，哀毀骨立，世稱其孝。

translations.literal: He left office for his father's mourning — his grief destroyed him to the bone — the age called him filial.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father — grief wasted him to the bone — men called him filial.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，知其清正，引為錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, knowing his integrity, he took him on as Recording Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was Chancellor, knowing his integrity, he made him Recording Advisor.

sentences.zh: 遷掌朝大夫，從行軍總管是雲暉擊叛蠻，以功拜儀同。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master Who Holds Court and followed Army Inspector-General Shiyun Hui in attacking rebellious barbarians — for merit he was granted Commissioner with Distinction.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand Master Who Holds Court and followed Army Inspector-General Shiyun Hui against rebellious barbarians — for merit he received Commissioner with Distinction.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，授大理丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen accepted the Mandate, he was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Chao became Assistant Director of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 處法平允，考績連最。

translations.literal: His application of the law was fair and even; his performance evaluations were continuously top-ranked.
translations.idiomatic: He applied the law fairly; his evaluations were always top-ranked.

sentences.zh: 曆大理正、尚書都官侍郎，每有奏讞，正色侃然，漸見禮重。

translations.literal: He successively served as Directing Secretary of the Court of Judicial Review and Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice — whenever he submitted judgments he was stern and upright in countenance and gradually came to be treated with ceremony and weight.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Directing Secretary of Judicial Review and Vice Director of Justice — stern at every judgment, he won growing respect.

sentences.zh: 上以盜賊不禁，將重其法，綽進諫曰：「律者天下之大信，其可失乎！

translations.literal: The emperor, because bandits and thieves were not stopped, was about to make the law heavier — Chao remonstrated saying: "The law is the great trust of the realm — can it be lost!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to toughen the law because theft would not stop — Chao remonstrated: "Law is the realm's great trust — it cannot be lost!

sentences.zh: 」上忻然納之，因謂曰：「若更有聞見，宜數言之。

translations.literal: " The emperor gladly accepted and therefore said: "If you have further observations, you should speak of them often.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor gladly accepted and said, "If you see more, speak often.

sentences.zh: 」遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: " He became Vice Director of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 故陳將蕭摩訶，其子世略在江南作亂，摩訶當從坐。

translations.literal: Former Chen general Xiao Mohe — his son Shilue raised rebellion in the Jiangnan — Mohe was to be implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: Former Chen general Xiao Mohe's son Shilue rebelled in the south — Mohe was to be punished by association.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「世略年未二十，亦何能為！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Shilue is not yet twenty — what can he do!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shilue is not yet twenty — what could he do?

sentences.zh: 以其名將之子，為人逼耳。

translations.literal: Because he is the son of a famous general, men forced him — that is all.
translations.idiomatic: He is a famous general's son — men forced him, that is all.

sentences.zh: 」因赦摩訶。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Mohe was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: " Mohe was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 綽固諫不可，上不能奪，欲待綽去而赦之，因命綽退食。

translations.literal: Chao firmly remonstrated that it could not be done — the emperor could not override him; he wished to wait until Chao left and then pardon him, and therefore ordered Chao to withdraw for his meal.
translations.idiomatic: Chao insisted it could not stand — the emperor could not override him and planned to pardon Mohe once Chao left, ordering Chao to withdraw for his meal.

sentences.zh: 綽曰：「臣奏獄未決，不敢退朝。

translations.literal: Chao said: "Your servant's memorial on the case is not yet decided — I dare not withdraw from court.
translations.idiomatic: Chao said, "My case is not yet decided — I dare not leave court.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「大理其為朕特放摩訶也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Let the Court of Judicial Review specially pardon Mohe for me.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Let Judicial Review specially pardon Mohe for me.

sentences.zh: 」因命左右釋之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered attendants to release him.
translations.idiomatic: " Attendants released him.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎辛亶嘗衣緋褌，俗雲利官，上以為厭蠱，將斬之，綽曰：「據法不當死，臣不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments Xin Dan once wore red trousers — common talk said they brought official profit — the emperor took it for sorcery and was about to behead him; Chao said: "According to the law he should not die — your servant dare not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xin Dan wore red trousers — folk said they brought office; the emperor took it for sorcery and meant to behead him; Chao said, "By law he should not die — I dare not obey.

sentences.zh: 」上怒甚，謂曰：「卿惜辛亶而不自惜也？

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly enraged and said: "You spare Xin Dan but do not spare yourself?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor raged: "You spare Xin Dan but not yourself?

sentences.zh: 」命左僕射高熲將綽斬之。

translations.literal: " He ordered Left Vice Director Gao Jiong to behead Chao.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Left Vice Director Gao Jiong to execute Chao.

sentences.zh: 綽曰：「陛下寧可殺臣，不可殺辛亶。

translations.literal: Chao said: "Your Majesty may kill your servant — you cannot kill Xin Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Chao said, "Your Majesty may kill me — you cannot kill Xin Dan.

sentences.zh: 」至朝堂，解衣當斬。

translations.literal: " Reaching the court hall, he removed his robe to await execution.
translations.idiomatic: " At the court hall he stripped for execution.

sentences.zh: 上使人謂綽曰：「竟如何？

translations.literal: The emperor sent a man to ask Chao: "After all, what then?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent to ask, "Well?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「執法一心，不敢惜死。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Upholding the law with single-mindedness — I dare not spare death.
translations.idiomatic: " Chao answered, "I uphold the law with all my heart — I do not fear death.

sentences.zh: 」上拂衣入，良久乃釋之。

translations.literal: " The emperor brushed his robe and entered; after a long time he released him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor turned away; after a long while he released him.

sentences.zh: 明日，謝綽，勞勉之，賜物三百段。

translations.literal: The next day he apologized to Chao, commended and encouraged him, and granted three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he apologized, encouraged Chao, and gave three hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 時上禁行惡錢，有二人在市以惡錢易好者，武候執以聞，上悉令斬之。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor forbade the circulation of debased coin — two men in the market exchanged debased coin for good coin; military guards seized them and reported; the emperor ordered all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor banned debased coin — two men in the market traded bad coin for good; guards reported them; the emperor ordered all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 綽諫曰：「此人坐當杖，殺之非法。

translations.literal: Chao remonstrated: "These men's offense warrants the cudgel — to kill them is against the law.
translations.idiomatic: Chao remonstrated: "Their crime warrants beating — killing them is unlawful.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「不關卿事。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "It does not concern you.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "It is none of your business.

sentences.zh: 」綽曰：「陛下不以臣愚暗，置在法司，欲妄殺人，豈得不關臣事？

translations.literal: " Chao said: "Your Majesty, not considering your servant stupid and dark, placed him in the legal office — if you wish to kill men wrongly, how can it not concern your servant's office?
translations.idiomatic: " Chao said, "You placed me in the legal office — if you kill wrongly, how is it not my business?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「撼大木不動者，當退。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "When one shakes a great tree and it does not move, one should withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "When a great tree will not shake, one should step back.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣望感天心，何論動木！

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your servant hopes to move the heart of Heaven — what talk of moving trees!
translations.idiomatic: " Chao replied, "I hope to move Heaven's heart — what talk of trees!

sentences.zh: 」上復曰：「啜羹者，熱則置之。

translations.literal: " The emperor again said: "One who sips broth — when it is hot, sets it aside.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said again, "One who sips hot broth sets it aside.

sentences.zh: 天子之感，欲相挫邪？

translations.literal: Does the Son of Heaven's feeling wish to be thwarted?
translations.idiomatic: Does the Son of Heaven wish to be thwarted?

sentences.zh: 」綽拜而益前，訶之不肯退。

translations.literal: " Chao bowed and advanced further, reproaching him and refusing to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: " Chao bowed, advanced, reproached him, and would not withdraw.

sentences.zh: 上遂入。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon entered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withdrew.

sentences.zh: 書侍御史柳彧復上奏切諫，上乃止。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary and Censor Liu Yu again submitted a memorial remonstrating sharply — the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Liu Yu submitted another sharp remonstrance — the emperor then stopped.

sentences.zh: 上以綽有誠直之心，每引入閣中，或遇上與皇后同榻，即呼綽坐，評論得失。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Chao had a sincere and straight heart, often brought him into the inner chambers — sometimes when he met the emperor and empress on the same couch, he would call Chao to sit and discuss successes and failures.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chao was sincere and straight, the emperor often brought him into the inner chambers — even when emperor and empress shared a couch, he called Chao to sit and discuss policy.

sentences.zh: 前後賞賜以萬計。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards over time numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 後進開府，贈其父為蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was advanced to Opening the Office; his father was posthumously granted Prefect of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received Opening the Office; his father was posthumously made Prefect of Cai.

sentences.zh: 時河東薛胄為大理卿，俱名平恕。

translations.literal: At that time Xue Zhou of Hedong was Director of the Court of Judicial Review — both were known for fairness and leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhou of Hedong was then Director of Judicial Review — both were known for fairness.

sentences.zh: 然胄斷獄以情，而綽守法，俱為稱職。

translations.literal: Yet Zhou decided cases by sentiment, while Chao upheld the law — both were called competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou decided cases by circumstance; Chao upheld the law — both were called competent.

sentences.zh: 上每謂綽曰：「朕於卿無所愛惜，但卿骨相不當貴耳。

translations.literal: The emperor often said to Chao: "I have nothing I would not give you — but your bone structure is not suited for high honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often told Chao, "I would withhold nothing from you — but your bone structure is not suited to high rank.

sentences.zh: 」仁壽中，卒官，上為之流涕，中使弔祭，鴻臚監護喪事。

translations.literal: " In the Renshou era he died in office; the emperor wept for him, sent palace envoys to mourn and sacrifice, and the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Renshou era he died in office; the emperor wept, sent envoys to mourn, and the Director of Imperial Sacrifices supervised the funeral.

sentences.zh: 二子元方、元襲。

translations.literal: Two sons: Yuanfang and Yuanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yuanfang and Yuanxi.

sentences.zh: 杜整，字皇育，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Du Zheng, courtesy name Huangyu, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zheng, styled Huangyu, came from Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖盛，魏潁川太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sheng was Prefect of Yingchuan in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Du Sheng was Prefect of Yingchuan under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父辟，渭州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Pi was Prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Du Pi was Prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 整少有風概，九歲丁父憂，哀毀骨立，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: From youth Zheng had bearing and spirit; at nine he entered mourning for his father — his grief destroyed him to the bone — he served his mother and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zheng had spirit; at nine he mourned his father — grief wasted him to the bone — and he was known for filial service to his mother.

sentences.zh: 及長，驍勇有膂力，好讀《孫吳兵法》。

translations.literal: When grown he was brave and had physical strength, fond of reading Sun Wu's Art of War.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was brave and strong, fond of reading Sun Wu's Art of War.

sentences.zh: 魏大統末，襲爵武鄉侯。

translations.literal: At the end of Great Unity of Wei he inherited the title Marquis of Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei's Great Unity he inherited the title Marquis of Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 周文引為親信。

translations.literal: Wen of Zhou took him on as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou took him as a trusted intimate.

sentences.zh: 累遷儀同三司、武州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Third Rank Commissioner with Distinction and Prefect of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Third Rank Commissioner with Distinction and Prefect of Wu.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，加上儀同，進爵平原縣公，入為勳曹中大夫。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, he was given the additional rank of Commissioner with Distinction, advanced to Duke of Pingyuan, and entered court as Grand Master of Meritorious Achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, he received Commissioner with Distinction, was made Duke of Pingyuan, and entered court as Grand Master of Meritorious Achievement.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，進位開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, his rank was advanced to Opening the Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, he received Opening the Office.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，加上開府，進封長廣郡公，拜左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor accepted the Mandate, he was given Upper Opening the Office, advanced to Duke of Changguang Commandery, and appointed General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, he received Upper Opening the Office, was made Duke of Changguang, and appointed General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 開皇六年，突厥犯塞，詔衛王爽北伐，以整為行軍總管，兼元帥長史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaihuang, the Turks raided the frontier — an edict ordered Prince of Wei Shuang on a northern campaign; Zheng was made Army Inspector-General and concurrently Chief of Staff to the commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 6 the Turks raided the frontier — Prince of Wei Shuang was ordered north; Zheng was Army Inspector-General and Chief of Staff.

sentences.zh: 至合川，無虜而還。

translations.literal: Reaching Hechuan, there were no barbarians and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Hechuan he found no enemy and returned.

sentences.zh: 密進取陳策，上善之，以為行軍總管，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: He secretly submitted a strategy to take Chen — the emperor approved and made him Army Inspector-General, garrisoning Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly submitted a strategy against Chen — the emperor approved and made him Army Inspector-General at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，上傷之，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He died; the emperor grieved and posthumously titled him Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died; the emperor grieved and posthumously titled him Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子楷嗣，位開府。

translations.literal: His son Kai inherited the title, holding the rank of Opening the Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kai inherited the title with the rank of Opening the Office.

sentences.zh: 整弟肅，亦有志行，位北地太守。

translations.literal: Zheng's younger brother Su also had will and conduct, holding the post of Prefect of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's younger brother Su also had will and integrity, serving as Prefect of Beidi.

sentences.zh: 論曰：大廈之構，非一本之枝，帝王之功，非一士之略，長短殊用，大小異宜，郐咨棁棟樑，莫可棄也。

translations.literal: The commentators say: The great hall's construction is not a single branch — the emperor's achievement is not a single man's strategy; long and short have different uses, great and small different fitness — rafters, purlins, beams, and ridgepoles — none may be cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: A great hall needs more than one beam — an emperor's achievement needs more than one man's strategy; long and short serve different ends, great and small fit different roles — rafters, purlins, beams, ridgepoles — none may be discarded.

sentences.zh: 裴政、李諤、鮑宏、高構、榮毗、陸知命等，或文能道義，或才足幹時，識用顯于當年，故事留於台閣。

translations.literal: Pei Zheng, Li E, Bao Hong, Gao Gou, Rong Pi, Lu Zhiming, and others — some were literarily able to convey moral principle, some talented enough to serve the age — their insight and employment were displayed in their time, their deeds preserved in the archives.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zheng, Li E, Bao Hong, Gao Gou, Rong Pi, Lu Zhiming, and others — some conveyed moral principle in writing, some had talent to serve the age — all distinguished in their time, their deeds preserved in the archives.

sentences.zh: 參之有隋多士，取其開物成務，皆廊廟之榱桷，亦北辰之眾星也。

translations.literal: Count them among Sui's many scholars — take their opening things and completing tasks — all are rafters of the hall, also the many stars of the Northern Pole.
translations.idiomatic: Among Sui's many scholars they opened things and completed tasks — all rafters of the state, stars of the Northern Pole.

sentences.zh: 趙綽居大理，囹圄無冤。

translations.literal: Zhao Chao presided over the Court of Judicial Review — the prisons held no wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chao presided over Judicial Review — no innocent languished in prison.

sentences.zh: 柳彧之處憲台，奸邪自肅。

translations.literal: Liu Yu at the Censorate — the wicked and corrupt corrected themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu at the Censorate — the wicked corrected themselves.

sentences.zh: 然不畏禦，梁毗得之矣。

translations.literal: Yet not fearing the imperial will — Lian Pi attained this.
translations.idiomatic: Not fearing the throne — Lian Pi attained this.

sentences.zh: 邦之司直，柳彧近之矣。

translations.literal: The state's straight officer — Liu Yu came near to it.
translations.idiomatic: The state's straight officer — Liu Yu came near.

sentences.zh: 杜整以聲績著美，其有以取之乎！

translations.literal: Du Zheng won beauty through reputation and achievement — did he not have what it takes!
translations.idiomatic: Du Zheng won renown through achievement — did he not earn it!
